Observed throughput: **one bead per ~40 minutes**, with three separate interventions required (priority bump, stale-assignee clear, worker restarts). Pinned workers (`claim_auto` on a home workspace) processed hundreds of beads on the same host during the same window.\n10\t\n11\tRoot causes, verified in code and worker logs:\n12\t\n13\t1. **Return-on-first-candidates deadlock.** `ExploreStrand::evaluate` (src/strand/explore.rs) iterates a static workspace list in filesystem-discovery order and returns at the first workspace with ready candidates. Worker-level exclusions (race-lost TTL 30s) and unclaimable assignees are applied *after* the strand returns. A workspace whose candidates are all unclaimable therefore satisfies \"has candidates\" every cycle, the worker nets zero, sleeps the idle backoff (900s observed), and never advances to workspace #2. One poisoned store starves the entire estate.\n14\t2. **Thundering herd.** Every worker walks the same list in the same order — all roamers converge on the same hot store, race for the same bead, and the losers idle.\n15\t3. **Store-layer limit bugs.** The `br ready --json` invocation passes no `--limit` (bead-forge's default limit truncates priority-sorted output — low-priority beads become invisible in busy stores) and another path passes `--limit 0`, which returns an empty set on deployed bead-forge 0.2.0. This produced both \"P3 beads invisible\" and the persistent `bf list failed` log noise.\n16\t4. **Stale assignees are permanent.** `candidates.retain(|b| b.assignee.is_none())` is correct as a claim guard, but nothing ever *releases* a stale assignee on an **open** bead (bead-forge `reopen` does not clear assignee; cross-workspace mend only handles orphaned in-progress beads). A reopened bead became permanently unclaimable by every worker.\n17\t5. **Claim errors masquerade as races.** CLI claim failures collapse into `claimed_by=(race)`, so version-skew or store corruption presents as endless quiet race losses instead of a loud error.\n18\t6. **Boot-only discovery.** The workspace list is captured at construction and never refreshed (a deliberate v1 constraint), so newly created stores require worker restarts.\n19\t\n20\t## Decision\n21\t\n22\tHarden the explore strand along six axes (plan.md Phase 5):\n23\t\n24\t1. **Claimable-aware filtering** — pass worker exclusion state into the strand's `Filters` so scan advancement is driven by *claimable-by-me* candidates, eliminating the deadlock class.\n25\t2. **Per-worker scan rotation** — start iteration at `hash(qualified_id) % N` to de-herd workers across stores.\n26\t3. **Explicit store limits + version handshake** — never rely on CLI default or zero limits; WARN at boot on known-bad bead-forge versions.\n27\t4. **Mend heals open+assigned beads** — clear assignees whose workers have no live heartbeat. (The root fix — `reopen` clears assignee — belongs in bead-forge; NEEDLE stays defensive regardless.)\n28\t5. **Claim-error taxonomy** — distinguish error from race; escalate repeated errors via telemetry instead of silent cycling.\n29\t6. **Event-driven cadence + periodic re-discovery + starvation telemetry** — inotify/mtime wakeups on `issues.jsonl` with a jittered 60–120s floor; found-but-excluded triggers short retry, never idle backoff; re-run workspace discovery periodically; emit per-cycle scan summaries and a \"ready beads exist but nothing claimed for X minutes\" alarm.\n30\t\n31\tKept from v1 by design: no upward traversal; workers return home after one remote bead; explicit `workspaces` config overrides discovery.\n32\t\n33\t## Consequences\n34\t\n35\t- Roam mode becomes a dependable dispatch path; fleet-wide sweeps (one bead in each of N repos) stop requiring per-repo pinned workers and manual babysitting.\n36\t- Slightly more store traffic (shorter polling floor, re-discovery) — bounded by jitter and mtime pre-checks, and far cheaper than the operator interventions it replaces.\n37\t- New telemetry events extend the existing schema (additive; JSONL/OTLP consumers unaffected).\n38\t- The starvation alarm gives FABRIC/HOOP a signal for the fleet-immune-system layer identified in the 2026-07 corpus audit.\n39\t- Until bead-forge ships the `reopen`-clears-assignee and `--limit 0` fixes, NEEDLE carries defensive workarounds (assignee healing, explicit limits) that can later be simplified.\n40\t\n41\t## Evidence\n42\t\n43\t- Lab worker logs 2026-07-11 20:51–21:22Z: `strand found candidates strand=explore candidates=2 excluded=2` repeating against a single workspace; Worker-level exclusions (race-lost TTL 30s) and unclaimable assignees are applied *after* the strand returns. A workspace whose candidates are all unclaimable therefore satisfies \"has candidates\" every cycle, the worker nets zero, sleeps the idle backoff (900s observed), and never advances to workspace #2. One poisoned store starves the entire estate.\n2. **Thundering herd.** Every worker walks the same list in the same order — all roamers converge on the same hot store, race for the same bead, and the losers idle.\n3. **Store-layer limit bugs.** The `br ready --json` invocation passes no `--limit` (bead-forge's default limit truncates priority-sorted output — low-priority beads become invisible in busy stores) and another path passes `--limit 0`, which returns an empty set on deployed bead-forge 0.2.0. This produced both \"P3 beads invisible\" and the persistent `bf list failed` log noise.\n4. **Stale assignees are permanent.** `candidates.retain(|b| b.assignee.is_none())` is correct as a claim guard, but nothing ever *releases* a stale assignee on an **open** bead (bead-forge `reopen` does not clear assignee; cross-workspace mend only handles orphaned in-progress beads). A reopened bead became permanently unclaimable by every worker.\n5. **Claim errors masquerade as races.** CLI claim failures collapse into `claimed_by=(race)`, so version-skew or store corruption presents as endless quiet race losses instead of a loud error.\n6. **Boot-only discovery.** The workspace list is captured at construction and never refreshed (a deliberate v1 constraint), so newly created stores require worker restarts.\n\n## Decision\n\nHarden the explore strand along six axes (plan.md Phase 5):\n\n1. **Claimable-aware filtering** — pass worker exclusion state into the strand's `Filters` so scan advancement is driven by *claimable-by-me* candidates, eliminating the deadlock class.\n2. **Per-worker scan rotation** — start iteration at `hash(qualified_id) % N` to de-herd workers across stores.\n3. **Explicit store limits + version handshake** — never rely on CLI default or zero limits; WARN at boot on known-bad bead-forge versions.\n4. **Mend heals open+assigned beads** — clear assignees whose workers have no live heartbeat. (The root fix — `reopen` clears assignee — belongs in bead-forge; NEEDLE stays defensive regardless.)\n5. **Claim-error taxonomy** — distinguish error from race; escalate repeated errors via telemetry instead of silent cycling.\n6. **Event-driven cadence + periodic re-discovery + starvation telemetry** — inotify/mtime wakeups on `issues.jsonl` with a jittered 60–120s floor; found-but-excluded triggers short retry, never idle backoff; re-run workspace discovery periodically; emit per-cycle scan summaries and a \"ready beads exist but nothing claimed for X minutes\" alarm.\n\nKept from v1 by design: no upward traversal; workers return home after one remote bead; explicit `workspaces` config overrides discovery.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Roam mode becomes a dependable dispatch path; fleet-wide sweeps (one bead in each of N repos) stop requiring per-repo pinned workers and manual babysitting.\n- Slightly more store traffic (shorter polling floor, re-discovery) — bounded by jitter and mtime pre-checks, and far cheaper than the operator interventions it replaces.\n- New telemetry events extend the existing schema (additive; JSONL/OTLP consumers unaffected).\n- The starvation alarm gives FABRIC/HOOP a signal for the fleet-immune-system layer identified in the 2026-07 corpus audit.\n- Until bead-forge ships the `reopen`-clears-assignee and `--limit 0` fixes, NEEDLE carries defensive workarounds (assignee healing, explicit limits) that can later be simplified.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- Lab worker logs 2026-07-11 20:51–21:22Z: `strand found candidates strand=explore candidates=2 excluded=2` repeating against a single workspace; `claim race lost ... claimed_by=(race)`; 900s idle loops.\n- Throughput comparison, same host, same hour: roamers 1 bead/40 min; pinned workers ~40 beads/hour.\n- bead-forge 0.2.0 `--limit 0` returns empty (known bug, fixed at HEAD, unreleased at time of writing).\n","numLines":46,"startLine":1,"totalLines":46}}}

discover_workspaces(root: &Path) -> Vec<PathBuf> {\n        let mut discovered = Vec::new();\n\n        // If root doesn't exist, return empty (not an error).\n        if !root.exists() {\n            tracing::debug!(root = %root.display(), \"workspace root does not exist, no workspaces discovered\");\n            return discovered;\n        }\n\n        // Read the directory; non-existent or /// Check if a workspace path has a `.beads/` directory.\n    fn has_beads_dir(workspace: &Path) -> bool {\n        workspace.join(\".beads\").is_dir()\n    }\n\n    /// Create a BrCliBeadStore for a Every design decision in this plan traces back to one or more of them.\n8\t\n9\t1. **Deterministic order.** Given the same queue state, every worker computes the same bead ordering. There is no randomness in selection. Ties are broken by creation time.\n10\t\n11\t2. **Explicit outcome paths.** Every possible result of every operation has a named handler. If an outcome can happen, it has a handler. If it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen. The type system enforces exhaustiveness.\n12\t\n13\t3. **Platform and model agnostic.** NEEDLE wraps any headless CLI that accepts a prompt and exits. It runs on any POSIX system. It does not depend on any specific AI provider, model, or API.\n14\t\n15\t4. **Observable by default.** Every state transition, claim attempt, dispatch, and outcome emits structured telemetry. A silent worker is a broken worker. Telemetry is structured from origin (JSONL) and exportable as OpenTelemetry (OTLP) so any compliant backend — Tempo, Jaeger, Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, FABRIC — can consume NEEDLE's signals without a custom adapter.\n16\t\n17\t5. **Self-healing.** Workers detect and recover from stuck states, stale claims, crashed peers, and corrupted databases without human intervention. Recovery paths are explicit, not heuristic.\n18\t\n19\t6. **Separation of concerns.** The orchestrator does not execute work. The agent does not manage state. The bead store does not enforce workflow. Each component has one job.\n20\t\n21\t---\n22\t\n23\t## Architecture Overview\n24\t\n25\tNEEDLE is composed of five layers:\n26\t\n27\t```\n28\t┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n29\t│                        CLI Layer                              │\n30\t│  needle run | stop | list | attach | status | config          │\n31\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n32\t│                     Worker Layer                              │\n33\t│  Worker loop, strand waterfall, session management            │\n34\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n35\t│                  Coordination Layer                            │\n36\t│  Claiming, locking, heartbeats, peer awareness                │\n37\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n38\t│                    Agent Layer                                 │\n39\t│  Adapter interface, dispatch, result capture                  │\n40\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n41\t│                   Foundation Layer                             │\n42\t│  Telemetry, configuration, bead store interface, self-healing │\n43\t└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n44\t```\n45\t\n46\t### Component Map\n47\t\n48\t| Component | Responsibility | Inputs | Outputs |\n49\t|-----------|---------------|--------|---------|\n50\t| **CLI** | Parse commands, manage sessions | User commands | Worker processes |\n51\t| **Worker** | Execute the strand waterfall loop | Bead queue state | Dispatch requests, state transitions |\n52\t| **StrandRunner** | Evaluate strands in sequence | Queue state, **OutcomeHandler** | Route exit code to explicit handler | Exit code, stdout/stderr | State transition |\n57\t| **Telemetry** | Structured event emission | Any component event | JSONL records |\n58\t| **HealthMonitor** | Heartbeat, stuck detection, peer awareness | Worker state | Recovery actions |\n59\t| **ConfigLoader** | Hierarchical config resolution | Files, env, CLI args | Resolved config |\n60\t| **BeadStore** | Abstract interface to bead backend | CRUD operations | Bead records |\n61\t| **Mitosis** | Split multi-task beads into children with dedup | Failed bead, parent's existing children | Child beads or no-op |\n62\t\n63\t---\n64\t\n65\t## Language Decision\n66\t\n67\tThe implementation language must provide:\n68\t\n69\t| Requirement | Why | Source |\n70\t|-------------|-----|--------|\n71\t| Exhaustive pattern matching | Every outcome must be handled; compiler enforces it | Principle 2, bead-lifecycle-bugs.md |\n72\t| Real module system | 45K single-file bash was unmaintainable | bash-at-scale-problems.md |\n73\t| Structured error types | Silent failures caused cascading bugs | claim-race-conditions.md |\n74\t| Native JSON support | Fragile jq parsing corrupted state | worker-starvation-lessons.md |\n75\t| Proper concurrency primitives | flock/trap/PID files were inadequate | concurrency-approaches-compared.md |\n76\t| Single binary distribution | NEEDLE must be trivially installable | Principle 3 |\n77\t| Cross-platform | Linux, macOS at minimum | Principle 3 |\n78\t| Static analysis | Catch undefined functions, unused variables at compile time | bundler-build-integrity.md |\n79\t\n80\t**Recommended: Rust.** Exhaustive `match`, `Result<T, E>` error handling, `serde_json`, `tokio` for async, single binary via static linking, cross-compilation. The beads ecosystem already has Rust precedent (beads_rust, beads-polis).\n81\t\n82\t**Acceptable alternative: Go.** Simpler learning curve, good concurrency, single binary. Lacks exhaustive matching (requires discipline instead of compiler enforcement).\n83\t\n84\t**Not acceptable: Bash, Python, Node.** Bash failed at scale (documented). Python/Node require runtime dependencies, violating single-binary distribution.\n85\t\n86\t---\n87\t\n88\t## Key Decisions from Research\n89\t\n90\tThese decisions are informed by the 14 research files in `docs/research/`:\n91\t\n92\t| Decision | Chosen Approach | Alternative Considered | Why |\n93\t|----------|----------------|----------------------|-----|\n94\t| Bead store interface | Abstract trait over `br` CLI | Direct SQLite access | Platform agnostic; works with future bead backends |\n95\t| Claim atomicity | `br update --claim` + workspace flock | Central coordinator (Perles) | No SPOF; works with decentralized workers |\n96\t| Heartbeat model | File-based heartbeat with TTL (from beads-polis) | Shared memory | Survives worker crashes; observable by peers |\n97\t| Validation gates | Pluggable gate system (inspired by bg-gate) | Hardcoded checks | Different workspaces need different validation |\n98\t| Work decomposition | Built-in mitosis with child-aware dedup | External only (spec2beads) | Mitosis is valid when the split criteria are semantic (multi-task detection) and dedup checks the parent's existing children |\n99\t| Self-modification | Allowed with release channel promotion (testing → stable → fleet hot-reload) | Prohibited entirely | v1 failures came from untested changes deploying directly to the fleet. Canary testing with defined inputs/outputs prevents this. |\n100\t| Workspace discovery | Explicit configuration | Filesystem scanning | Explore strand's unbounded find caused 35+ load |\n101\t| Alert system | Verify-then-alert with rate limiting | Alert-on-empty | 100% false positive rate from naive alerting |\n102\t\n103\t## Key Decisions from Operational Learnings\n104\t\n105\tThese decisions are informed by the 9 notes files in `docs/notes/`:\n106\t\n107\t| Learning | Design Response |\n108\t|----------|----------------|\n109\t| Mitosis explosion (5,741 duplicate beads) | Mitosis checks parent's existing children before creating new ones. Duplicate splits are structurally impossible. Split criteria are semantic (multi-task detection), not numeric. |\n110\t| 100% false positive starvation alerts | Three-state model: no beads exist / all claimed / invisible. Verify independently before alerting. |\n111\t| Bundler shipped undefined functions | Compiled language eliminates this class entirely. |\n112\t| Agent-owned closure most reliable | NEEDLE does not close beads. Agent receives `br close <id>` instruction in prompt. |\n113\t| stdout/stderr corruption | Telemetry is a structured system, never interleaved with agent output. |\n114\t| Workers modifying their own orchestrator | Self-modification allowed via release channels. New builds must pass canary tests in isolation before promotion to `:stable`. Fleet hot-reloads from `:stable`, never from `:testing`. |\n115\t| ~20 worker practical limit (EX44) | Fleet sizing is bounded by three runtime factors: provider inference throughput, available CPU, and available RAM. NEEDLE monitors these and warns when saturated. Staggered launch is default. |\n116\t| Bead granularity affects success rate | Document guidelines but don't enforce — this is a bead authoring concern, not orchestration. |\n117\t\n118\t---\n119\t\n120\t# State Machine\n121\t\n122\tThe worker loop is a finite state machine.
