`estimated_cost_usd` |\n1805\t\n1806\t## Sinks\n1807\t\n1808\tTelemetry events are dispatched to one or more sinks. Sinks are configured independently.\n1809\t\n1810\t### File Sink (default, always on)\n1811\t\n1812\tWrites JSONL to per-worker log files:\n1813\t\n1814\t```\n1815\t~/.needle/logs/<worker-id>.jsonl\n1816\t```\n1817\t\n1818\t- One line per event\n1819\t- File is append-only\n1820\t- Rotation: new file per session (session ID in filename) or size-based (configurable)\n1821\t\n1822\t### Stdout Sink (optional)\n1823\t\n1824\tWrites human-readable summary to stdout for interactive monitoring:\n1825\t\n1826\t```\n1827\t15:30:00 [alpha] CLAIMED nd-a3f8 (p1: \"Fix auth middleware\")\n1828\t15:30:02 [alpha] DISPATCHED claude-sonnet pid=12345\n1829\t15:32:15 [alpha] SUCCESS nd-a3f8 (135s, ~2400 tokens)\n1830\t15:32:15 [alpha] CLAIMED nd-b2c9 (p2: \"Add rate limiting tests\")\n1831\t```\n1832\t\n1833\t- Enabled when worker runs in foreground or via `needle attach`\n1834\t- Format is configurable: `minimal`, `normal`, `verbose`\n1835\t- Color-coded by event type\n1836\t\n1837\t### Hook Sink (optional)\n1838\t\n1839\tDispatches events to external systems via webhook or command:\n1840\t\n1841\t```yaml\n1842\ttelemetry:\n1843\t  hooks:\n1844\t    - event_filter: \"outcome.*\"\n1845\t      command: \"curl -X POST https://webhook.example.com/needle -d @-\"\n1846\t    - event_filter: \"worker.errored\"\n1847\t      command: \"/path/to/alert-script.sh\"\n1848\t    - event_filter: \"effort.recorded\"\n1849\t      command: \"/path/to/cost-tracker.sh\"\n1850\t```\n1851\t\n1852\t- Events matching the filter are piped as JSON to the command's stdin\n1853\t- Hook execution is fire-and-forget (non-blocking)\n1854\t- Failed hooks emit a `telemetry.hook.failed` event to the file sink (not recursively to hooks)\n1855\t\n1856\t### OTLP Sink (optional)\n1857\t\n1858\tExports telemetry as OpenTelemetry signals (traces, metrics, logs) over OTLP to any compliant collector (OpenTelemetry Collector, Jaeger, Tempo, Grafana Alloy, Honeycomb, Datadog, etc.). This is the canonical integration point for FABRIC and any downstream observability plane.\n1859\t\n1860\t```yaml\n1861\ttelemetry:\n1862\t  otlp:\n1863\t    enabled: true\n1864\t    endpoint: \"http://otel-collector.tailnet:4317\"    # gRPC default; use 4318 for HTTP\n1865\t    protocol: grpc                                     # grpc | http/protobuf\n1866\t    headers:\n1867\t      authorization: \"Bearer ${OTEL_TOKEN}\"            # env interpolation\n1868\t    timeout_ms: 5000\n1869\t    compression: gzip                                  # none | gzip\n1870\t    tls:\n1871\t      insecure: false\n1872\t      ca_file: \"\"\n1873\t    signals:\n1874\t      traces: true\n1875\t      metrics: true\n1876\t      logs: true\n1877\t    resource_attributes:\n1878\t      deployment.environment: \"production\"\n1879\t      service.namespace: \"needle-fleet\"\n1880\t```\n1881\t\n1882\tDesign:\n1883\t\n1884\t- **Non-blocking.** Uses a batch span/log/metric processor. If the collector is unreachable, events are buffered up to a bounded queue, then dropped (same policy as file sink). Drops emit a `telemetry.otlp.dropped` event to the file sink (never recursively to OTLP).\n1885\t- **Additive.** The file sink is authoritative. OTLP is an export, not a replacement. If OTLP is disabled or misconfigured, NEEDLE behaves identically to a file-sink-only deployment.\n1886\t- **Stdlib deps.** Rust crates: `opentelemetry`, `opentelemetry_sdk`, `opentelemetry-otlp`, `opentelemetry-semantic-conventions`. All support OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP.\n1887\t- **W3C trace context.** Trace and span IDs are generated per the W3C Trace Context spec so they interop with any OTel backend.\n1888\t- **Graceful shutdown.** On `worker.stopped`, the exporter is flushed with a deadline before process exit. Failure to flush is logged but never blocks shutdown.\n1889\t\n1890\t## OpenTelemetry Semantic Mapping\n1891\t\n1892\tNEEDLE's existing event catalog maps cleanly to OpenTelemetry's three signal types. This mapping is **normative** — the OTLP sink implementation must conform to it so dashboards and alerts remain stable across NEEDLE versions.\n1893\t\n1894\t### Resource Attributes\n1895\t\n1896\tEvery exported signal carries these resource attributes (per OTel semantic conventions):\n1897\t\n1898\t| Attribute | Value | Source |\n1899\t|-----------|-------|--------|\n1900\t| `service.name` | `\"needle\"` | Constant |\n1901\t| `service.version` | build version | `env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\")` |\n1902\t| `service.instance.id` | `<worker_id>` | e.g., `needle-claude-anthropic-sonnet-alpha` |\n1903\t| `service.namespace` | `\"needle-fleet\"` (default, configurable) | Config |\n1904\t| `deployment.environment` | e.g., `\"production\"` | Config |\n1905\t| `host.name` | hostname | OS |\n1906\t| `process.pid` | worker PID | OS |\n1907\t| `needle.agent` | e.g., `\"claude-anthropic-sonnet\"` | Worker config |\n1908\t| `needle.model` | e.g., `\"claude-sonnet-4-6\"` | Worker config |\n1909\t| `needle.session_id` | session ID | Per-boot random |\n1910\t| `needle.workspace` | workspace path | Worker config |\n1911\t\n1912\t### Traces\n1913\t\n1914\tThe NEEDLE state machine is naturally hierarchical, which maps directly to OTel spans.\n1915\t\n1916\t```\n1917\tworker.session                                          (root span, lifetime = worker process)\n1918\t├── strand.pluck                                        (one per strand evaluation)\n1919\t│   └── bead.lifecycle                                  (one per claimed bead)\n1920\t│       ├── bead.claim                                  (ATOMIC phase)\n1921\t│       ├── bead.prompt_build\n1922\t│       ├── agent.dispatch                              (DISPATCHING + EXECUTING)\n1923\t│       │   └── agent.execution                         (process alive; span.ok on exit 0)\n1924\t│       └── bead.outcome                                (HANDLING)\n1925\t│           └── bead.mitosis?                           (optional, if outcome = failure)\n1926\t├── strand.mend\n1927\t├── strand.explore\n1928\t├── strand.weave\n1929\t├── strand.unravel\n1930\t├── strand.pulse\n1931\t└── strand.knot                                         (terminal backoff / exhaustion)\n1932\t```\n1933\t\n1934\tSpan naming follows OpenTelemetry conventions: lowercase dotted, verb-form where appropriate.\n1935\t\n1936\t**Span attributes** follow OTel semantic conventions where applicable, plus a `needle.*` namespace:\n1937\t\n1938\t| Span | Key Attributes |\n1939\t|------|----------------|\n1940\t| `worker.session` | `needle.beads_processed`, `needle.uptime_seconds`, `needle.exit_reason` |\n1941\t| `strand.*` | `needle.strand.name`, `needle.strand.result`, `needle.strand.duration_ms` |\n1942\t| `bead.lifecycle` | `needle.bead.id`, `needle.bead.priority`, `needle.bead.title_hash`, `needle.bead.outcome` |\n1943\t| `bead.claim` | `needle.claim.retry_number`, `needle.claim.result` (`succeeded` / `race_lost` / `failed`) |\n1944\t| `agent.dispatch` | `gen_ai.system` (e.g., `anthropic`), `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`, `needle.agent.pid`, `needle.agent.exit_code` |\n1945\t| `bead.outcome` | `needle.outcome` (`success` / `failure` / `timeout` / `crash` / `agent_not_found` / `interrupted`), `needle.outcome.action` |\n1946\t\n1947\t**GenAI semantic conventions.** The `agent.dispatch` span uses OTel's `gen_ai.*` conventions so NEEDLE's token/cost data shows up in GenAI dashboards out-of-the-box (Grafana GenAI app, Langfuse, Honeycomb AI, etc.).\n1948\t\n1949\t**Span status.** Success outcomes set `Status::Ok`. All other outcomes set `Status::Error` with a description matching the `needle.outcome` value. This makes error-rate SLOs trivial.\n1950\t\n1951\t**Context propagation.** The trace ID from `worker.session` is recorded in the file-sink event envelope as a new optional field `trace_id`, enabling correlation between the JSONL file sink and the OTel backend without ambiguity.\n1952\t\n1953\t### Metrics\n1954\t\n1955\tMetrics are emitted via the OTel Meter API, one `Meter` per worker.
