|\n| `bead.orphaned` | Agent exited 0 but bead still open | `bead_id` |\n\n### Agent Dispatch\n\n| Event Type | Emitted When | Data Fields |\n|------------|-------------|-------------|\n| `agent.dispatched` | Agent process started | `agent_name`, `model`, `pid`, `prompt_hash`, `prompt_tokens_est` |\n| `agent.executing` | Periodic during execution | `pid`, `elapsed_ms`, `still_alive` |\n| `agent.completed` | Agent process exited | `exit_code`, `elapsed_ms`, `stdout_bytes`, `stderr_bytes` |\n| `agent.timeout` | Agent killed for timeout | `timeout_ms`, `pid` |\n\n### Outcome Handling\n\n| Event Type | Emitted When | Data Fields |\n|------------|-------------|-------------|\n| `outcome.classified` | Exit code mapped to outcome | `outcome` (`success`, `failure`, `timeout`, `crash`, `agent_not_found`, `interrupted`), `exit_code` |\n| `outcome.handled` | Handler executed | `outcome`, `action` (`released`, `deferred`, `alerted`, `none`) |\n\n### Health\n\n| Event Type | Emitted When | Data Fields |\n|------------|-------------|-------------|\n| `heartbeat.emitted` | Heartbeat file updated | `state`, `current_bead` |\n| `peer.stale` | Stale peer detected | `peer_id`, `last_seen`, `claimed_bead` |\n| `peer.crashed` | Dead peer cleaned up | `peer_id`, `released_bead` |\n| `health.check` | Periodic health check | `db_healthy`, `disk_free_mb`, `peer_count` |\n| `fleet.cpu_saturated` | System load exceeds threshold | `load_average` (f64), `threshold` (f64), `core_count` (usize) |\n| `fleet.memory_low` | Free memory below threshold | `free_mb` (u64), `threshold_mb` (u64) |\n\n### Effort Tracking\n\n| Event Type | Emitted When | Data Fields |\n|------------|-------------|-------------|\n| `effort.recorded` | After each bead processing cycle | `bead_id`, `elapsed_ms`, `agent_name`, `model`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `estimated_cost_usd` |\n\n## Sinks\n\nTelemetry events are dispatched to one or more sinks. Sinks are configured independently.\n\n### File Sink (default, always on)\n\nWrites JSONL to per-worker log files:\n\n```\n~/.needle/logs/<worker-id>.jsonl\n```\n\n- One line per event\n- File is append-only\n- Rotation: new file per session (session ID in filename) or size-based (configurable)\n\n### Stdout Sink (optional)\n\nWrites human-readable summary to stdout for interactive monitoring:\n\n```\n15:30:00 [alpha] CLAIMED nd-a3f8 (p1: \"Fix auth middleware\")\n15:30:02 [alpha] DISPATCHED claude-sonnet pid=12345\n15:32:15 [alpha] SUCCESS nd-a3f8 (135s, ~2400 tokens)\n15:32:15 [alpha] CLAIMED nd-b2c9 (p2: \"Add rate limiting tests\")\n```\n\n- Enabled when worker runs in foreground or via `needle attach`\n- Format is configurable: `minimal`, `normal`, `verbose`\n- Color-coded by event type\n\n### Hook Sink (optional)\n\nDispatches events to external systems via webhook or command:\n\n```yaml\ntelemetry:\n  hooks:\n    - event_filter: \"outcome.*\"\n      command: \"curl -X POST https://webhook.example.com/needle -d @-\"\n    - event_filter: \"worker.errored\"\n      command: \"/path/to/alert-script.sh\"\n    - event_filter: \"effort.recorded\"\n      command: \"/path/to/cost-tracker.sh\"\n```\n\n- Events matching the filter are piped as JSON to the command's stdin\n- Hook execution is fire-and-forget (non-blocking)\n- Failed hooks emit a `telemetry.hook.failed` event to the file sink (not recursively to hooks)\n\n### OTLP Sink (optional)\n\nExports telemetry as OpenTelemetry signals (traces, metrics, logs) over OTLP to any compliant collector (OpenTelemetry Collector, Jaeger, Tempo, Grafana Alloy, Honeycomb, Datadog, etc.). This is the canonical integration point for FABRIC and any downstream observability plane.\n\n```yaml\ntelemetry:\n  otlp:\n    enabled: true\n    endpoint: \"http://otel-collector.tailnet:4317\"    # gRPC default; use 4318 for HTTP\n    protocol: grpc                                     # grpc | http/protobuf\n    headers:\n      authorization: \"Bearer ${OTEL_TOKEN}\"            # env interpolation\n    timeout_ms: 5000\n    compression: gzip                                  # none | gzip\n    tls:\n      insecure: false\n      ca_file: \"\"\n    signals:\n      traces: true\n      metrics: true\n      logs: true\n    resource_attributes:\n      deployment.environment: \"production\"\n      service.namespace: \"needle-fleet\"\n```\n\nDesign:\n\n- **Non-blocking.** Uses a batch span/log/metric processor. If the collector is unreachable, events are buffered up to a bounded queue, then dropped (same policy as file sink). Drops emit a `telemetry.otlp.dropped` event to the file sink (never recursively to OTLP).\n- **Additive.** The file sink is authoritative. OTLP is an export, not a replacement. If OTLP is disabled or misconfigured, NEEDLE behaves identically to a file-sink-only deployment.\n- **Stdlib deps.** Rust crates: `opentelemetry`, `opentelemetry_sdk`, `opentelemetry-otlp`, `opentelemetry-semantic-conventions`. All support OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP.\n- **W3C trace context.** Trace and span IDs are generated per the W3C Trace Context spec so they interop with any OTel backend.\n- **Graceful shutdown.** On `worker.stopped`, the exporter is flushed with a deadline before process exit. Failure to flush is logged but never blocks shutdown.\n\n## OpenTelemetry Semantic Mapping\n\nNEEDLE's existing event catalog maps cleanly to OpenTelemetry's three signal types. This mapping is **normative** — the OTLP sink implementation must conform to it so dashboards and alerts remain stable across NEEDLE versions.\n\n### Resource Attributes\n\nEvery exported signal carries these resource attributes (per OTel semantic conventions):\n\n| Attribute | Value | Source |\n|-----------|-------|--------|\n| `service.name` | `\"needle\"` | Constant |\n| `service.version` | build version | `env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\")` |\n| `service.instance.id` | `<worker_id>` | e.g., `needle-claude-anthropic-sonnet-alpha` |\n| `service.namespace` | `\"needle-fleet\"` (default, configurable) | Config |\n| `deployment.environment` | e.g., `\"production\"` | Config |\n| `host.name` | hostname | OS |\n| `process.pid` | worker PID | OS |\n| `needle.agent` | e.g., `\"claude-anthropic-sonnet\"` | Worker config |\n| `needle.model` | e.g., `\"claude-sonnet-4-6\"` | Worker config |\n| `needle.session_id` | session ID | Per-boot random |\n| `needle.workspace` | workspace path | Worker config |\n\n### Traces\n\nThe NEEDLE state machine is naturally hierarchical, which maps directly to OTel spans.\n\n```\nworker.session                                          (root span, lifetime = worker process)\n├── strand.pluck                                        (one per strand evaluation)\n│   └── bead.lifecycle                                  (one per claimed bead)\n│       ├── bead.claim                                  (ATOMIC phase)\n│       ├── bead.prompt_build\n│       ├── agent.dispatch                              (DISPATCHING + EXECUTING)\n│       │   └── agent.execution                         (process alive; span.ok on exit 0)\n│       └── bead.outcome                                (HANDLING)\n│           └── bead.mitosis? All other outcomes set `Status::Error` with a description matching the `needle.outcome` value. This makes error-rate SLOs trivial.\n\n**Context propagation.** The trace ID from `worker.session` is recorded in the file-sink event envelope as a new optional field `trace_id`, enabling correlation between the JSONL file sink and the OTel backend without ambiguity.\n\n### Metrics\n\nMetrics are emitted via the OTel Meter API, one `Meter` per worker. All metrics are prefixed `needle.*`.\n\n| Metric | Instrument | Unit | Attributes | Description |\n|--------|-----------|------|------------|-------------|\n| `needle.workers.active` | UpDownCounter | `{worker}` | — | Current live worker count (incremented on `worker.started`, decremented on `worker.stopped`) |\n| `needle.beads.claimed` | Counter | `{bead}` | `strand`, `priority` | Successful bead claims |\n| `needle.beads.completed` | Counter | `{bead}` | `outcome` | Bead terminal outcomes (one per `bead.outcome`) |\n| `needle.beads.duration` | Histogram | `ms` | `outcome` | End-to-end bead lifecycle time |\n| `needle.claim.attempts` | Counter | `{attempt}` | `result` (`succeeded`/`race_lost`/`failed`) | Claim attempts |\n| `needle.strand.duration` | Histogram | `ms` | `strand`, `result` | Strand evaluation time |\n| `needle.agent.duration` | Histogram | `ms` | `agent`, `model`, `exit_code` | Agent process runtime |\n| `needle.agent.tokens.input` | Counter | `{token}` | `agent`, `model` | Input tokens consumed |","numLines":1966,"startLine":1,"totalLines":3988,"truncatedByTokenCap":true}}}

This is agent-specific and best-effort:\n1997\t\n1998\t| Agent | Extraction Method |\n1999\t|-------|-------------------|\n2000\t| Claude Code | Parse `--output-format json` for `usage.input_tokens`, `usage.output_tokens` |\n2001\t| OpenCode | Parse structured output (TBD) |\n2002\t| Codex CLI | Parse structured output (TBD) |\n2003\t| Aider | Parse cost summary line from stderr |\n2004\t| Generic | No extraction; record elapsed time only |\n2005\t\n2006\tIf token extraction fails, the event is still emitted with `null` token fields. Missing tokens are not an error.\n2007\t\n2008\t### Cost Estimation\n2009\t\n2010\tCost is estimated from tokens using configurable per-model pricing:\n2011\t\n2012\t```yaml\n2013\tpricing:\n2014\t  claude-sonnet:\n2015\t    input_per_million: 3.00\n2016\t    output_per_million: 15.00\n2017\t  claude-opus:\n2018\t    input_per_million: 15.00\n2019\t    output_per_million: 75.00\n2020\t  gpt-4:\n2021\t    input_per_million: 30.00\n2022\t    output_per_million: 60.00\n2023\t```\n2024\t\n2025\tCost is **estimated**, never authoritative. It is recorded in telemetry for trend analysis, not for billing.\n2026\t\n2027\t## Querying Telemetry\n2028\t\n2029\tNEEDLE includes built-in telemetry queries via the CLI:\n2030\t\n2031\t```bash\n2032\t# Summary of today's work\n2033\tneedle status\n2034\t\n2035\t# Per-worker breakdown\n2036\tneedle status --by-worker\n2037\t\n2038\t# Cost summary\n2039\tneedle status --cost --since 2026-03-20\n2040\t\n2041\t# Event stream (tail -f equivalent)\n2042\tneedle logs --follow\n2043\t\n2044\t# Filter by event type\n2045\tneedle logs --filter \"bead.claim.*\" --since 1h\n2046\t\n2047\t# Export for external analysis\n2048\tneedle logs --format jsonl --since 24h > export.jsonl\n2049\t```\n2050\t\n2051\t---\n2052\t\n2053\t# Self-Healing\n2054\t\n2055\tNEEDLE workers must detect and recover from failures without human intervention. This section specifies the failure modes, detection mechanisms, and recovery procedures.\n2056\t\n2057\t## Failure Taxonomy\n2058\t\n2059\t| Failure | Scope | Detection | Recovery |\n2060\t|---------|-------|-----------|----------|\n2061\t| Worker crash | Worker | Heartbeat TTL expiry | Peer cleanup via Mend |\n2062\t| Worker stuck | Worker | Heartbeat stale + PID alive | Alert via Knot |\n2063\t| Agent hang | Bead | Execution timeout | Kill process, release bead |\n2064\t| Stale claim | Bead | in_progress + no heartbeat | Mend releases bead |\n2065\t| Orphaned lock | Workspace | Lock file age > TTL | Mend removes lock |\n2066\t| Database corruption | Workspace | `br doctor` detects | Auto-repair from JSONL |\n2067\t| Stale dependency | Bead | Closed bead still blocks open bead | Mend cleans dependency |\n2068\t| Disk full | System | Write failure | Emit alert, graceful stop |\n2069\t| Bead store unreachable | System | `br` command fails | Retry with backoff, then stop |\n2070\t\n2071\t## Heartbeat-Based Detection\n2072\t\n2073\t```\n2074\tWorker A (alive)          Worker B (alive)         Worker C (crashed)\n2075\t┌──────────────┐         ┌──────────────┐         ┌──────────────┐\n2076\t│ heartbeat:   │         │ heartbeat:   │         │ heartbeat:   │\n2077\t│ 15:30:00     │         │ 15:30:10     │         │ 15:20:00     │ ← stale\n2078\t│ state: EXEC  │         │ state: SEL   │         │ state: EXEC  │\n2079\t│ bead: nd-a3f │         │ bead: null   │         │ bead: nd-x7y │ ← orphaned claim\n2080\t└──────────────┘         └──────────────┘         └──────────────┘\n2081\t\n2082\tWorker B runs Mend strand:\n2083\t  1. Reads all heartbeat files\n2084\t  2. Detects C's heartbeat is stale (10 min old, TTL is 5 min)\n2085\t  3. Checks PID: dead\n2086\t  4. Releases nd-x7y: br update nd-x7y --status open --unassign\n2087\t  5. Removes C's heartbeat file\n2088\t  6. Deregisters C from worker registry\n2089\t  7. Emits peer.crashed telemetry\n2090\t```\n2091\t\n2092\t### Detection Parameters\n2093\t\n2094\t| Parameter | Default | Description |\n2095\t|-----------|---------|-------------|\n2096\t| `heartbeat_interval` | 30s | How often a worker writes its heartbeat |\n2097\t| `heartbeat_ttl` | 5min | How long before a heartbeat is considered stale |\n2098\t| `peer_check_interval` | 60s | How often Mend checks peer heartbeats |\n2099\t\n2100\t**Relationship:** `heartbeat_ttl` should be at least `3 × heartbeat_interval` to tolerate transient delays.\n2101\t\n2102\t### Stuck vs. Crashed\n2103\t\n2104\t| Signal | Diagnosis | Action |\n2105\t|--------|-----------|--------|\n2106\t| Stale heartbeat + PID dead | **Crashed.** Worker terminated unexpectedly. | Release claim, clean up, emit `peer.crashed` |\n2107\t| Stale heartbeat + PID alive | **Stuck.** Worker is hung (deadlock, infinite loop, blocked I/O). | Emit `peer.stale` warning. Do NOT kill — may be legitimately slow. Alert via Knot after threshold. |\n2108\t| Fresh heartbeat + PID alive | **Healthy.** Normal operation. | No action. |\n2109\t\n2110\t**NEEDLE does not auto-kill stuck workers.** A stuck worker with a live PID may be executing a legitimately slow agent. Killing it would interrupt work. Instead, NEEDLE alerts via Knot and lets the human decide.\n2111\t\n2112\t## Database Recovery\n2113\t\n2114\tbeads_rust uses SQLite with a known corruption issue (FrankenSQLite, upstream #171). NEEDLE must handle this.\n2115\t\n2116\t### Recovery Procedure\n2117\t\n2118\t```\n2119\tCorruption detected\n2120\t       │\n2121\t       ▼\n2122\t  Run br doctor --repair\n2123\t       │\n2124\t       ├── Success ──► Resume operation, emit health.db_repaired\n2125\t       │\n2126\t       └── Failure ──► Full rebuild:\n2127\t                          1. rm .beads/beads.db\n2128\t                          2. br sync --import\n2129\t                          3. Verify: br doctor\n2130\t                          │\n2131\t                          ├── Success ──► Resume, emit health.db_rebuilt\n2132\t                          │\n2133\t                          └── Failure ──► ERRORED state (JSONL itself may be corrupt)\n2134\t```\n2135\t\n2136\t**Key insight from `docs/notes/mitosis-explosion-postmortem.md`:** The JSONL file is always the authoritative data source. It is append-only and immune to SQLite corruption. Recovery always rebuilds from JSONL.\n2137\t\n2138\t### Proactive Health Checks\n2139\t\n2140\tThe Mend strand runs `br doctor` (without `--repair`) periodically:\n2141\t- After every N beads processed (configurable, default: 50)\n2142\t- On every Mend strand evaluation\n2143\t- If doctor reports warnings, escalate to `--repair` immediately rather than waiting for failure\n2144\t\n2145\t## Stale Claim Recovery\n2146\t\n2147\t```\n2148\tMend strand evaluates:\n2149\t  1. Query beads with status=in_progress\n2150\t  2. For each:\n2151\t     a. Read assigned worker ID from bead\n2152\t     b. Check worker's heartbeat file\n2153\t     c. If heartbeat is stale AND PID is dead:\n2154\t        - br update <bead_id> --status open --unassign\n2155\t        - Emit bead.released telemetry (reason: stale_claim)\n2156\t     d. If heartbeat is stale AND PID is alive:\n2157\t        - Emit peer.stale warning (do not release — worker may be slow)\n2158\t     e. If heartbeat is fresh:\n2159\t        - Normal operation, skip\n2160\t```\n2161\t\n2162\tA claimed bead is only released if the owning worker is **confirmed dead** (stale heartbeat AND dead PID). If the PID is alive, the bead is not released, even if the heartbeat is stale.\n2163\t\n2164\t## Lock File Recovery\n2165\t\n2166\tMend strand checks lock file age:\n2167\t1. Read lock files in `/tmp/needle-claim-*.lock`\n2168\t2. If file modification time > `lock_ttl` (default: 10 minutes):\n2169\t   - Attempt to acquire flock (non-blocking)\n2170\t   - If acquired: no one holds it, delete the file, release flock\n2171\t   - If not acquired: someone is actively holding it, skip\n2172\t\n2173\t## Dependency Link Recovery\n2174\t\n2175\tMend strand checks for stale dependencies:\n2176\t1. Query beads with status `open` that have blockers\n2177\t2. For each blocker, check if the blocking bead is closed\n2178\t3. If blocker is closed, remove the dependency link\n2179\t4. Emit `bead.dependency.cleaned` telemetry\n2180\t\n2181\tThis is a necessary compensating mechanism because `br` does not automatically resolve dependency links on bead closure (documented in `docs/notes/bead-lifecycle-bugs.md`).\n2182\t\n2183\t## Graceful Degradation\n2184\t\n2185\tWhen subsystems fail, NEEDLE degrades gracefully rather than crashing:\n2186\t\n2187\t| Subsystem Failure | Degradation |\n2188\t|-------------------|-------------|\n2189\t| Telemetry file sink unwritable | Buffer events in memory, retry. If buffer full, drop events. Worker continues. |\n2190\t| Heartbeat file unwritable | Log error. Worker continues but cannot be monitored by peers. If persistent, ERRORED. |\n2191\t| Worker registry unwritable | Log error. Worker continues but invisible to `needle list`. |\n2192\t| Database corrupt | Auto-repair. If repair fails, ERRORED for that workspace only. |\n2193\t| Single workspace unreachable | Skip workspace in Explore, continue with others. |\n2194\t| Config file unreadable mid-session | Use cached config from boot. Emit warning. |\n2195\t\n2196\t## Self-Modification and Release Channels\n2197\t\n2198\tNEEDLE workers are allowed to modify NEEDLE itself. The v1 failures (see `docs/notes/self-modification-risks.md`) were not caused by self-modification as a concept — they were caused by untested changes deploying directly to the running fleet. The solution is not to ban self-modification but to gate promotion through release channels with canary testing.\n2199\t\n2200\t### Release Channels\n2201\t\n2202\t```\n2203\t:testing ──► :stable ──► fleet hot-reload\n2204\t                │\n2205\t                └── rollback to previous :stable on failure\n2206\t```\n2207\t\n2208\tThree channels:\n2209\t\n2210\t| Channel | Purpose | Who writes | Who reads |\n2211\t|---------|---------|------------|-----------|\n2212\t| `:testing` | Newly built binary, not yet validated | Worker that built it | Canary test harness only |\n2213\t| `:stable` | Validated binary, approved for fleet use | Promotion pipeline (after canary passes) | Running fleet via hot-reload |\n2214\t| `:latest` | Alias for the most recent `:stable` | Automatic on promotion | `needle upgrade` default target |\n2215\t\n2216\t### Canary Testing Pipeline\n2217\t\n2218\tWhen a worker modifies NEEDLE's source and builds a new binary:\n2219\t\n2220\t```\n2221\tWorker builds new binary\n2222\t       │\n2223\t       ▼\n2224\t  Install as :testing\n2225\t  (~/.needle/bin/needle-testing)\n2226\t       │\n2227\t       ▼\n2228\t  Run canary test suite:\n2229\t    1. Launch :testing binary with test .beads/ directory\n2230\t    2. Test beads have defined inputs and expected outcomes\n2231\t    3. :testing processes beads in isolation\n2232\t    4. Compare actual outcomes against expected\n2233\t       │\n2234\t       ├── All pass → Promote :testing to :stable\n2235\t       │                 │\n2236\t       │                 ▼\n2237\t       │              Fleet detects new :stable\n2238\t       │              Workers hot-reload on next bead boundary\n2239\t       │\n2240\t       └── Any fail → Reject :testing\n2241\t                        │\n2242\t                        ▼\n2243\t                     Mark bead as failed\n2244\t                     :stable remains unchanged\n2245\t                     Fleet continues on previous :stable\n2246\t                     Emit canary.failed telemetry\n2247\t```\n2248\t\n2249\t### Canary Test Suite\n2250\t\n2251\tThe canary suite is a set of test beads with known-good outcomes stored in a dedicated test workspace:\n2252\t\n2253\t```\n2254\t~/.needle/canary/\n2255\t├── .beads/                    # test bead store\n2256\t│   ├── issues.jsonl\n2257\t│   └── beads.db\n2258\t├── test-workspace/            # mock workspace with source files\n2259\t│   ├── src/\n2260\t│   │   └── hello.py           # simple file for beads to modify\n2261\t│   └── .beads/\n2262\t└── expected/                  # expected outcomes per bead\n2263\t    ├── bead-001.expected.json # { \"exit_code\": 0, \"bead_closed\": true }\n2264\t    ├── bead-002.expected.json # { \"exit_code\": 0, \"files_modified\": [\"src/hello.py\"] }\n2265\t    └── bead-003.expected.json # { \"exit_code\": 1, \"bead_closed\": false }\n2266\t```\n2267\t\n2268\tTest beads cover:\n2269\t- **Happy path:** Simple bead that should succeed and close\n2270\t- **Failure path:** Bead that should fail (tests outcome handling)\n2271\t- **Timeout path:** Bead with intentionally slow agent (tests timeout enforcement)\n2272\t- **State machine integrity:** Verify telemetry events match expected state transitions\n2273\t- **Mitosis:** Multi-task bead that should split on failure\n2274\t\n2275\t### Hot-Reload Protocol\n2276\t\n2277\tRunning workers check for a new `:stable` binary between bead processing cycles (after LOGGING, before SELECTING):\n2278\t\n2279\t1. Compare current binary hash against `:stable` binary hash\n2280\t2. If different:\n2281\t   a. Emit `worker.upgrade.detected` telemetry\n2282\t   b. Complete current bead cycle (never interrupt mid-execution)\n2283\t   c. Re-exec with the new binary: `exec ~/.needle/bin/needle-stable run --resume`\n2284\t   d. New binary picks up worker state from heartbeat file and registry\n2285\t3. If same: continue normally\n2286\t\n2287\t**`--resume` flag:** Tells the new binary to inherit the worker's identity (ID, session, tmux) rather than creating a new session. The worker continues from the SELECTING state with a fresh binary.\n2288\t\n2289\t### Rollback\n2290\t\n2291\tIf a promoted `:stable` causes failures in the fleet:\n2292\t\n2293\t1. Fleet workers emit `worker.errored` or repeated `outcome.failure` telemetry\n2294\t2. Human (or automated watchdog) runs: `needle rollback`\n2295\t3. Rollback restores the previous `:stable` from backup (`~/.needle/bin/needle-stable.prev`)\n2296\t4. Workers hot-reload to the rolled-back binary on next cycle\n2297\t\n2298\tRollback is always available because promotion preserves the previous `:stable` as a backup.\n2299\t\n2300\t### Binary Paths\n2301\t\n2302\t```\n2303\t~/.needle/bin/\n2304\t├── needle-testing             # candidate under canary evaluation\n2305\t├── needle-stable              # current fleet binary\n2306\t├── needle-stable.prev         # previous stable (rollback target)\n2307\t└── needle                     # symlink → needle-stable\n2308\t```\n2309\t\n2310\t### Configuration\n2311\t\n2312\t```yaml\n2313\tself_modification:\n2314\t  enabled: true                     # allow workers to process NEEDLE beads\n2315\t  canary_workspace: ~/.needle/canary  # test workspace with known-good beads\n2316\t  auto_promote: true                # promote to :stable automatically if canary passes\n2317\t  hot_reload: true                  # fleet hot-reloads from :stable between beads\n2318\t```\n2319\t\n2320\t### Telemetry\n2321\t\n2322\t| Event Type | Emitted When | Data Fields |\n2323\t|------------|-------------|-------------|\n2324\t| `canary.started` | Canary test suite begins | `testing_binary_hash`, `test_count` |\n2325\t| `canary.passed` | All canary tests passed | `testing_binary_hash`, `duration_ms` |\n2326\t| `canary.failed` | One or more canary tests failed | `testing_binary_hash`, `failures` (list) |\n2327\t| `promotion.completed` | :testing promoted to :stable | `old_hash`, `new_hash` |\n2328\t| `worker.upgrade.detected` | Worker sees new :stable | `old_hash`, `new_hash` |\n2329\t| `worker.upgrade.completed` | Worker re-exec'd with new binary | `new_hash` |\n2330\t| `rollback.completed` | :stable rolled back to previous | `rolled_back_hash`, `restored_hash` |\n2331\t\n2332\t---\n2333\t\n2334\t# Configuration\n2335\t\n2336\tNEEDLE uses a hierarchical configuration system. Values are resolved from highest to lowest precedence, with the first defined value winning.\n2337\t\n2338\t## Precedence Order\n2339\t\n2340\t```\n2341\tCLI arguments          (highest — overrides everything)\n2342\t       │\n2343\tEnvironment variables\n2344\t       │\n2345\tWorkspace config       (.needle.yaml in workspace root)\n2346\t       │\n2347\tGlobal config          (~/.needle/config.yaml)\n2348\t       │\n2349\tBuilt-in defaults      (lowest — always present)\n2350\t```\n2351\t\n2352\t**Rule:** A value set at a higher level completely replaces the lower level's value. There is no deep merging. For maps (like `strands`), the entire map is replaced, not merged key-by-key.\n2353\t\n2354\t**Exception:** The `workspaces` list in Explore strand config is additive — workspace configs can add to the global list but not remove from it.\n2355\t\n2356\t## Global Configuration\n2357\t\n2358\t**Location:** `~/.needle/config.yaml`\n2359\t\n2360\t```yaml\n2361\t# ── Agent Configuration ──\n2362\tagent:\n2363\t  default: claude-anthropic-sonnet\n2364\t  timeout: 600\n2365\t  adapters_dir: ~/.needle/agents\n2366\t\n2367\t# ── Worker Configuration ──\n2368\tworker:\n2369\t  max_workers: 0                      # 0 = no hard ceiling, rely on runtime monitoring\n2370\t  launch_stagger_seconds: 2\n2371\t  idle_timeout: 300\n2372\t  idle_action: wait\n2373\t  max_claim_retries: 5\n2374\t  identifier_scheme: nato\n2375\t  cpu_load_warn: 0.8                  # warn when load > 80% of cores\n2376\t  memory_free_warn_mb: 512            # warn when free RAM < 512MB\n2377\t\n2378\t# ── Workspace Configuration ──\n2379\tworkspace:\n2380\t  default: ~/projects/main\n2381\t  home: ~/projects/main\n2382\t\n2383\t# ── Strand Configuration ──\n2384\tstrands:\n2385\t  pluck:\n2386\t    enabled: true\n2387\t    exclude_labels: [deferred, human, blocked]\n2388\t  explore:\n2389\t    enabled: true\n2390\t    workspaces:\n2391\t      - ~/projects/api-server\n2392\t      - ~/projects/frontend\n2393\t  mend:\n2394\t    enabled: true\n2395\t    stale_claim_ttl: 300\n2396\t    lock_ttl: 600\n2397\t    db_check_interval: 50\n2398\t  weave:\n2399\t    enabled: false\n2400\t    max_beads_per_run: 5\n2401\t    cooldown_hours: 24\n2402\t    exclude_workspaces: []\n2403\t  unravel:\n2404\t    enabled: false\n2405\t    max_per_run: 3\n2406\t    cooldown_days: 7\n2407\t  pulse:\n2408\t    enabled: false\n2409\t    max_beads_per_run: 10\n2410\t    cooldown_hours: 48\n2411\t    severity_threshold: warning\n2412\t    scanners: []\n2413\t  knot:\n2414\t    enabled: true\n2415\t    alert_cooldown_minutes: 60\n2416\t    exhaustion_threshold: 3\n2417\t\n2418\t# ── Concurrency Limits ──\n2419\tlimits:\n2420\t  providers:\n2421\t    anthropic:\n2422\t      max_concurrent: 10\n2423\t      requests_per_minute: 60\n2424\t    openai:\n2425\t      max_concurrent: 5\n2426\t      requests_per_minute: 40\n2427\t  models: {}\n2428\t\n2429\t# ── Health Monitoring ──\n2430\thealth:\n2431\t  heartbeat_interval: 30\n2432\t  heartbeat_ttl: 300\n2433\t  peer_check_interval: 60\n2434\t\n2435\t# ── Telemetry ──\n2436\ttelemetry:\n2437\t  file_sink:\n2438\t    enabled: true\n2439\t    directory: ~/.needle/logs\n2440\t    rotation: session\n2441\t    retention_days: 30\n2442\t  stdout_sink:\n2443\t    enabled: false\n2444\t    format: normal\n2445\t    color: auto\n2446\t  hooks: []\n2447\t  otlp:\n2448\t    enabled: false\n2449\t    endpoint: \"http://localhost:4317\"\n2450\t    protocol: grpc              # grpc | http/protobuf\n2451\t    headers: {}                 # e.g., authorization: \"Bearer ${OTEL_TOKEN}\"\n2452\t    timeout_ms: 5000\n2453\t    compression: gzip           # none | gzip\n2454\t    tls:\n2455\t      insecure: false\n2456\t      ca_file: \"\"\n2457\t    signals:\n2458\t      traces: true\n2459\t      metrics: true\n2460\t      logs: true\n2461\t    resource_attributes:\n2462\t      deployment.environment: \"development\"\n2463\t      service.namespace: \"needle-fleet\"\n2464\t\n2465\t# ── Cost Tracking ──\n2466\tpricing: {}\n2467\tbudget:\n2468\t  warn_usd: 0\n2469\t  stop_usd: 0\n2470\t\n2471\t# ── Self-Modification & Release Channels ──\n2472\tself_modification:\n2473\t  enabled: true\n2474\t  canary_workspace: ~/.needle/canary\n2475\t  auto_promote: true\n2476\t  hot_reload: true\n2477\t```\n2478\t\n2479\t## Workspace Configuration\n2480\t\n2481\t**Location:** `.needle.yaml` in workspace root (next to `.beads/`)\n2482\t\n2483\tWorkspace-level configuration overrides global settings for that specific workspace. Only a subset of settings can be overridden at the workspace level.\n2484\t\n2485\t```yaml\n2486\tagent:\n2487\t  default: claude-anthropic-opus\n2488\t  timeout: 1200\n2489\t\n2490\tstrands:\n2491\t  weave:\n2492\t    enabled: true\n2493\t    max_beads_per_run: 3\n2494\t  pulse:\n2495\t    enabled: true\n2496\t    scanners:\n2497\t      - name: rust-clippy\n2498\t        command: \"cargo clippy --message-format=json 2>/dev/null\"\n2499\t\n2500\tprompt:\n2501\t  context_files:\n2502\t    - AGENTS.md\n2503\t    - docs/architecture.md\n2504\t  instructions: |\n2505\t    This workspace uses the repository pattern.\n2506\t    All database access must go through src/repository/.\n2507\t    Run `cargo test` before closing the bead.\n2508\t```\n2509\t\n2510\t### Overridable Settings\n2511\t\n2512\t| Setting | Workspace Override | Why |\n2513\t|---------|-------------------|-----|\n2514\t| `agent.default` | Yes | Different projects may need different models |\n2515\t| `agent.timeout` | Yes | Complex projects may need longer timeouts |\n2516\t| `strands.weave` | Yes | Some projects want gap analysis, others don't |\n2517\t| `strands.pulse` | Yes | Scanners are project-specific |\n2518\t| `strands.unravel` | Yes | Per-project opt-in |\n2519\t| `prompt.*` | Yes | Project-specific context and instructions |\n2520\t| `worker.*` | **No** | Worker config is fleet-level, not per-workspace |\n2521\t| `limits.*` | **No** | Rate limits are provider-level, not per-workspace |\n2522\t| `health.*` | **No** | Health monitoring is fleet-level |\n2523\t| `telemetry.*` | **No** | Telemetry config is fleet-level |\n2524\t\n2525\t## Environment Variables\n2526\t\n2527\tAll configuration keys can be overridden via environment variables with the `NEEDLE_` prefix. Nested keys use `__` (double underscore) as separator.\n2528\t\n2529\t| Config Key | Environment Variable |\n2530\t|------------|---------------------|\n2531\t| `agent.default` | `NEEDLE_AGENT__DEFAULT` |\n2532\t| `agent.timeout` | `NEEDLE_AGENT__TIMEOUT` |\n2533\t| `worker.max_workers` | `NEEDLE_WORKER__MAX_WORKERS` |\n2534\t| `strands.weave.enabled` | `NEEDLE_STRANDS__WEAVE__ENABLED` |\n2535\t\n2536\t## Configuration Validation\n2537\t\n2538\tConfiguration is validated at boot time. Invalid configuration causes the worker to enter ERRORED state immediately.\n2539\t\n2540\t### Required Fields\n2541\t\n2542\t- `agent.default` must reference a valid adapter (built-in or file exists in adapters dir)\n2543\t- `workspace.default` or `--workspace` must be a directory containing `.beads/`\n2544\t- Numeric fields must be positive\n2545\t- Duration fields must be > 0\n2546\t\n2547\t### Warnings (non-fatal)\n2548\t\n2549\t- `worker.max_workers` > 0 and > CPU count (consider runtime monitoring instead)\n2550\t- `health.heartbeat_ttl` < `3 * health.heartbeat_interval` (detection may be unreliable)\n2551\t- `strands.explore.workspaces` contains paths that don't exist\n2552\t- No pricing configured when `telemetry.effort.track_cost: true`\n2553\t\n2554\t### Config Dump\n2555\t\n2556\t```bash\n2557\tneedle config --dump\n2558\tneedle config --dump --show-source\n2559\t\n2560\t# Example output:\n2561\t# agent.default: claude-anthropic-sonnet (from: ~/.needle/config.yaml)\n2562\t# agent.timeout: 1200 (from: /home/coder/project/.needle.yaml)\n2563\t# worker.max_workers: 20 (from: NEEDLE_WORKER__MAX_WORKERS env var)\n2564\t# worker.idle_timeout: 300 (from: built-in default)\n2565\t```\n2566\t\n2567\t---\n2568\t\n2569\t# Agent Adapters\n2570\t\n2571\tNEEDLE is agent-agnostic. It wraps any headless CLI that accepts a prompt and exits. The adapter system is the abstraction layer that makes this possible.\n2572\t\n2573\tNEEDLE does not know how agents work. It knows how to:\n2574\t1. Render an invoke template with variables\n2575\t2. Pipe a prompt via the configured input method\n2576\t3. Wait for the process to exit\n2577\t4. Capture exit code, stdout, and stderr\n2578\t\n2579\tEverything else — authentication, model selection, context handling, tool use — is the agent's responsibility.\n2580\t\n2581\t## Adapter Interface\n2582\t\n2583\tAn adapter is a YAML file that describes how to invoke a specific agent:\n2584\t\n2585\t```yaml\n2586\tname: claude-anthropic-sonnet\n2587\tdescription: Claude Code with Anthropic Sonnet model\n2588\tagent_cli: claude\n2589\tversion_command: \"claude --version\"\n2590\tinput_method: stdin                   # stdin | file | args\n2591\tinvoke_template: >\n2592\t  cd {workspace} &&\n2593\t  claude --print\n2594\t  --model claude-sonnet-4-6\n2595\t  --max-turns 30\n2596\t  --output-format json\n2597\t  < {prompt_file}\n2598\tenvironment:\n2599\t  CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TURNS: \"30\"\n2600\ttoken_extraction:\n2601\t  method: json_field                  # json_field | regex | none\n2602\t  input_path: \"usage.input_tokens\"\n2603\t  output_path: \"usage.output_tokens\"\n2604\tprovider: anthropic\n2605\tmodel: claude-sonnet-4-6\n2606\t```\n2607\t\n2608\t## Input Methods\n2609\t\n2610\t### stdin\n2611\t\n2612\tPrompt is piped to the agent's stdin. Most common for Claude Code. NEEDLE writes the prompt to a temp file (`{prompt_file}`) and redirects it to stdin to avoid shell escaping issues.\n2613\t\n2614\t### file\n2615\t\n2616\tPrompt is written to a file and the file path is passed as an argument.\n2617\t\n2618\t### args\n2619\t\n2620\tPrompt is passed as a command-line argument. `{prompt_escaped}` is the prompt with shell metacharacters escaped. For long prompts, NEEDLE may fall back to file-based input.\n2621\t\n2622\t## Template Variables\n2623\t\n2624\t| Variable | Description | Example |\n2625\t|----------|-------------|---------|\n2626\t| `{workspace}` | Absolute path to workspace | `/home/coder/project` |\n2627\t| `{prompt_file}` | Path to temp file containing the prompt | `/tmp/needle-prompt-a1b2.txt` |\n2628\t| `{prompt_escaped}` | Shell-escaped prompt string | `Fix the auth bug in src/auth.rs` |\n2629\t| `{bead_id}` | Current bead ID | `nd-a3f8` |\n2630\t| `{model}` | Model identifier from adapter config | `claude-sonnet-4-6` |\n2631\t| `{worker_id}` | Worker identifier | `needle-claude-anthropic-sonnet-alpha` |\n2632\t| `{timeout}` | Timeout in seconds | `600` |\n2633\t\n2634\t## Built-in Adapters\n2635\t\n2636\tNEEDLE ships with adapters for common agents, embedded in the binary. These can be overridden by placing a file with the same name in `~/.needle/agents/`.\n2637\t\n2638\t### Claude Code (Sonnet)\n2639\t\n2640\t```yaml\n2641\tname: ([\\\\d,]+) received\"\n2711\t  input_group: 1\n2712\t  output_group: 2\n2713\tprovider: anthropic\n2714\tmodel: claude-sonnet-4-6\n2715\t```\n2716\t\n2717\t## Prompt Templates\n2718\t\n2719\tPrompts are configurable at both the global and workspace level. Every agent-invoking operation (Pluck execution, Weave gap analysis, Unravel alternatives, Pulse scanning, Mitosis splitting) uses a named prompt template. Templates are deterministic functions of their inputs — same bead state produces the same prompt.\n2720\t\n2721\t### Template Variables\n2722\t\n2723\tAll templates have access to these variables:\n2724\t\n2725\t| Variable | Available In | Description |\n2726\t|----------|-------------|-------------|\n2727\t| `{bead_id}` | All | Current bead ID |\n2728\t| `{bead_title}` | All | Bead title |\n2729\t| `{bead_body}` | All | Bead body/description |\n2730\t| `{workspace_path}` | All | Absolute path to workspace |\n2731\t| `{context_file_contents}` | All | Contents of configured context files |\n2732\t| `{workspace_instructions}` | All | Instructions from `.needle.yaml` |\n2733\t| `{worker_id}` | All | Worker identifier |\n2734\t| `{existing_children}` | Mitosis | Parent's current children (titles + IDs) |\n2735\t| `{human_bead_context}` | Unravel | The HUMAN-blocked bead being analyzed |\n2736\t| `{scan_results}` | Pulse | Output from configured scanners |\n2737\t| `{doc_files}` | Weave | Documentation file listing and contents |\n2738\t\n2739\t### Built-in Templates\n2740\t\n2741\t**`pluck` — Bead execution (default):**\n2742\t\n2743\t```markdown\n2744\t## Task\n2745\t\n2746\t{bead_title}\n2747\t\n2748\t## Description\n2749\t\n2750\t{bead_body}\n2751\t\n2752\t## Workspace\n2753\t\n2754\t{workspace_path}\n2755\t\n2756\t## Context Files\n2757\t\n2758\t{context_file_contents}\n2759\t\n2760\t## Instructions\n2761\t\n2762\t{workspace_instructions}\n2763\t\n2764\tComplete the task described above. When finished:\n2765\t- Commit your changes with a descriptive message\n2766\t- Close the bead: `br close {bead_id} --body \"Summary of what was done\"`\n2767\t\n2768\tIf you cannot complete the task:\n2769\t- Do NOT close the bead\n2770\t- The bead will be automatically released for retry\n2771\t\n2772\tBead ID: {bead_id}\n2773\t```\n2774\t\n2775\t**`mitosis` — Split analysis:**\n2776\t\n2777\t```markdown\n2778\t## Bead Analysis\n2779\t\n2780\tTitle: {bead_title}\n2781\tBody: {bead_body}\n2782\t\n2783\t## Existing Children\n2784\t\n2785\t{existing_children}\n2786\t\n2787\t## Question\n2788\t\n2789\tDoes this bead describe more than one independent task? A task is independent\n2790\tif it produces a distinct deliverable and could be completed without completing\n2791\tthe other tasks in this bead.\n2792\t\n2793\tIf yes, list each independent task as a structured child bead with:\n2794\t- title: concise task description\n2795\t- body: what needs to be done\n2796\t- dependencies: which other children must complete first (by title)\n2797\t\n2798\tIf this bead describes a single task (even a complex one), respond with: SINGLE_TASK\n2799\t\n2800\tDo not propose children that duplicate any existing children listed above.\n2801\t```\n2802\t\n2803\t**`weave` — Gap analysis:**\n2804\t\n2805\t```markdown\n2806\t## Workspace Documentation\n2807\t\n2808\t{doc_files}\n2809\t\n2810\t## Current Open Beads\n2811\t\n2812\t{existing_beads}\n2813\t\n2814\t## Question\n2815\t\n2816\tReview the documentation above. Identify gaps where documented features,\n2817\tAPIs, or workflows are incomplete, missing tests, or have no corresponding\n2818\timplementation bead.\n2819\t\n2820\tFor each gap found, propose a bead with:\n2821\t- title: concise description of what's missing\n2822\t- body: what needs to be done to close the gap\n2823\t- priority: 1 (critical), 2 (important), or 3 (nice-to-have)\n2824\t\n2825\tDo not propose beads that duplicate any existing open beads listed above.\n2826\tIf no gaps are found, respond with: NO_GAPS\n2827\t```\n2828\t\n2829\t**`unravel` — Alternative proposals:**\n2830\t\n2831\t```markdown\n2832\t## Blocked Bead\n2833\t\n2834\tTitle: {bead_title}\n2835\tBody: {bead_body}\n2836\tStatus: Blocked (requires human decision)\n2837\t\n2838\t## Question\n2839\t\n2840\tThis bead is blocked because it requires a human decision. Analyze the bead\n2841\tand propose alternative approaches that could be executed by an automated\n2842\tagent without the human decision.\n2843\t\n2844\tFor each alternative, provide:\n2845\t- title: concise description of the alternative approach\n2846\t- body: what would be done differently\n2847\t- tradeoffs: what is gained and what is lost compared to the original approach\n2848\t\n2849\tIf no viable alternatives exist, respond with: NO_ALTERNATIVES\n2850\t```\n2851\t\n2852\t**`pulse` — Health scan bead creation:**\n2853\t\n2854\t```markdown\n2855\t## Scan Results\n2856\t\n2857\t{scan_results}\n2858\t\n2859\t## Current Open Beads\n2860\t\n2861\t{existing_beads}\n2862\t\n2863\t## Question\n2864\t\n2865\tReview the scan results above. For issues that are significant enough to\n2866\twarrant a fix, propose a bead with:\n2867\t- title: concise description of the issue\n2868\t- body: what needs to be fixed and how\n2869\t- priority: based on severity (1=critical, 2=important, 3=minor)\n2870\t\n2871\tDo not propose beads that duplicate any existing open beads listed above.\n2872\tIf no significant issues are found, respond with: NO_ISSUES\n2873\t```\n2874\t\n2875\t### Overriding Templates\n2876\t\n2877\tTemplates are overridable at the workspace level in `.needle.yaml`:\n2878\t\n2879\t```yaml\n2880\tprompt:\n2881\t  context_files:\n2882\t    - CLAUDE.md\n2883\t    - AGENTS.md\n2884\t  instructions: |\n2885\t    This workspace uses the repository pattern.\n2886\t    Run `cargo test` before closing the bead.\n2887\t\n2888\t  templates:\n2889\t    pluck: |\n2890\t      {bead_title}\n2891\t\n2892\t      {bead_body}\n2893\t\n2894\t      Workspace: {workspace_path}\n2895\t      {context_file_contents}\n2896\t      {workspace_instructions}\n2897\t\n2898\t      Close when done: br close {bead_id} --body \"summary\"\n2899\t      Bead ID: {bead_id}\n2900\t\n2901\t    mitosis: |\n2902\t      ... custom mitosis prompt ...\n2903\t```\n2904\t\n2905\tIf a template is not overridden at the workspace level, the built-in default is used. Templates can also be overridden globally in `~/.needle/config.yaml` under `prompt.templates`.\n2906\t\n2907\t### Agent-Owned Closure\n2908\t\n2909\tThe pluck template instructs the agent to close the bead via `br close`. NEEDLE does not close beads itself. This is a deliberate design decision based on v1 experience:\n2910\t\n2911\t- The agent knows whether the work is actually done\n2912\t- NEEDLE's post-dispatch parsing of agent output was fragile\n2913\t- Exit code 0 does not guarantee the work was completed correctly\n2914\t- The agent can include a meaningful closure message\n2915\t\n2916\t## Adapter Validation\n2917\t\n2918\t```bash\n2919\tneedle test-agent claude-anthropic-sonnet\n2920\t\n2921\t# Output:\n2922\t#   Adapter: claude-anthropic-sonnet\n2923\t#   CLI:     claude (found at /home/coder/.local/bin/claude)\n2924\t#   Version: Claude Code v1.0.30\n2925\t#   Input:   stdin\n2926\t#   Probe:   echo hello → exit 0 (1.2s)\n2927\t#   Tokens:  extraction working (in: 45, out: 12)\n2928\t#   Status:  READY\n2929\t```\n2930\t\n2931\t## Adding a Custom Agent\n2932\t\n2933\t1. Create a YAML file in `~/.needle/agents/`\n2934\t2. Edit the file with the agent's invocation details\n2935\t3. Test the adapter: `needle test-agent my-agent`\n2936\t4. Use it: `needle run --agent my-agent`\n2937\t\n2938\tNo code changes required. No recompilation. No restart of other workers.\n2939\t\n2940\t---\n2941\t\n2942\t# Implementation Phases\n2943\t\n2944\tNEEDLE is built in three phases. Each phase produces a usable tool. No phase depends on future phases — Phase 1 alone is a complete, working system.\n2945\t\n2946\t## Phase 1: Core State Machine\n2947\t\n2948\t**Goal:** A single binary that processes beads from one workspace using one agent. The state machine is complete. Telemetry is complete. The tool works end-to-end.\n2949\t\n2950\t### Deliverables\n2951\t\n2952\t| Component | Scope |\n2953\t|-----------|-------|\n2954\t| **CLI** | `needle run`, `needle stop`, `needle list`, `needle sort beads from single workspace |\n2957\t| **Strand 7 (Knot)** | Basic exhaustion handling (backoff, exit) |\n2958\t| **Claimer** | Atomic claim via `br update --claim`, single workspace flock outcomes handled (success, failure, timeout, crash, agent_not_found, interrupted) |\n2962\t| **Telemetry** | File sink (JSONL), all events in catalog |\n2963\t| **Config** | Global config file, CLI argument overrides |\n2964\t| **Agent adapters** | Claude Code built-in, generic template |\n2965\t| **BeadStore** | `br` CLI wrapper with JSON parsing LogRecord with:\n\n- `severity_number` / `severity_text`: `INFO` for normal events, `WARN` for `peer.stale` / `telemetry.*.dropped`, `ERROR` for `worker.errored` / `bead.claim.failed` / `agent.timeout`.\n- `body`: the existing event `data` object.\n- `attributes`: flattened from the event envelope (`event_type`, `bead_id`, `workspace`, etc.).\n- `trace_id` / `span_id`: linked to the enclosing `bead.lifecycle` or `worker.session` span where applicable.\n\nEvents that ARE spans (e.g., `bead.claim.attempted` → a span, not a log) do not double-export as logs.\n\n### Span Events vs. Logs\n\nIntra-span state changes (e.g., `agent.executing` heartbeats, `heartbeat.emitted`) are recorded as OTel **span events** on the nearest enclosing span, not as separate logs. This keeps the signal count manageable and makes timelines in Tempo/Jaeger readable.\n\n## Token and Cost Tracking\n\n### Token Extraction\n\nNEEDLE attempts to extract token usage from agent output. This is agent-specific and best-effort:\n\n| Agent | Extraction Method |\n|-------|-------------------|\n| Claude Code | Parse `--output-format json` for `usage.input_tokens`, `usage.output_tokens` |\n| OpenCode | Parse structured output (TBD) |\n| Codex CLI | Parse structured output (TBD) |\n| Aider | Parse cost summary line from stderr |\n| Generic | No extraction; record elapsed time only |\n\nIf token extraction fails, the event is still emitted with `null` token fields. Missing tokens are not an error.\n\n### Cost Estimation\n\nCost is estimated from tokens using configurable per-model pricing:\n\n```yaml\npricing:\n  claude-sonnet:\n    input_per_million: 3.00\n    output_per_million: 15.00\n  claude-opus:\n    input_per_million: 15.00\n    output_per_million: 75.00\n  gpt-4:\n    input_per_million: 30.00\n    output_per_million: 60.00\n```\n\nCost is **estimated**, never authoritative. It is recorded in telemetry for trend analysis, not for billing.\n\n## Querying Telemetry\n\nNEEDLE includes built-in telemetry queries via the CLI:\n\n```bash\n# Summary of today's work\nneedle status\n\n# Per-worker breakdown\nneedle status --by-worker\n\n# Cost summary\nneedle status --cost --since 2026-03-20\n\n# Event stream (tail -f equivalent)\nneedle logs --follow\n\n# Filter by event type\nneedle logs --filter \"bead.claim.*\" --since 1h\n\n# Export for external analysis\nneedle logs --format jsonl --since 24h > export.jsonl\n```\n\n---\n\n# Self-Healing\n\nNEEDLE workers must detect and recover from failures without human intervention. This section specifies the failure modes, detection mechanisms, and recovery procedures.\n\n## Failure Taxonomy\n\n| Failure | Scope | Detection | Recovery |\n|---------|-------|-----------|----------|\n| Worker crash | Worker | Heartbeat TTL expiry | Peer cleanup via Mend |\n| Worker stuck | Worker | Heartbeat stale + PID alive | Alert via Knot |\n| Agent hang | Bead | Execution timeout | Kill process, release bead |\n| Stale claim | Bead | in_progress + no heartbeat | Mend releases bead |\n| Orphaned lock | Workspace | Lock file age > TTL | Mend removes lock |\n| Database corruption | Workspace | `br doctor` detects | Auto-repair from JSONL |\n| Stale dependency | Bead | Closed bead still blocks open bead | Mend cleans dependency |\n| Disk full | System | Write failure | Emit alert, graceful stop |\n| Bead store unreachable | System | `br` command fails | Retry with backoff, then stop |\n\n## Heartbeat-Based Detection\n\n```\nWorker A (alive)          Worker B (alive)         Worker C (crashed)\n┌──────────────┐         ┌──────────────┐         ┌──────────────┐\n│ heartbeat:   │         │ heartbeat:   │         │ heartbeat:   │\n│ 15:30:00     │         │ 15:30:10     │         │ 15:20:00     │ ← stale\n│ state: EXEC  │         │ state: SEL   │         │ state: EXEC  │\n│ bead: nd-a3f │         │ bead: null   │         │ bead: nd-x7y │ ← orphaned claim\n└──────────────┘         └──────────────┘         └──────────────┘\n\nWorker B runs Mend strand:\n  1. Reads all heartbeat files\n  2. Detects C's heartbeat is stale (10 min old, TTL is 5 min)\n  3. Checks PID: dead\n  4. Releases nd-x7y: br update nd-x7y --status open --unassign\n  5. Removes C's heartbeat file\n  6. Deregisters C from worker registry\n  7. Emits peer.crashed telemetry\n```\n\n### Detection Parameters\n\n| Parameter | Default | Description |\n|-----------|---------|-------------|\n| `heartbeat_interval` | 30s | How often a worker writes its heartbeat |\n| `heartbeat_ttl` | 5min | How long before a heartbeat is considered stale |\n| `peer_check_interval` | 60s | How often Mend checks peer heartbeats |\n\n**Relationship:** `heartbeat_ttl` should be at least `3 × heartbeat_interval` to tolerate transient delays.\n\n### Stuck vs. Crashed\n\n| Signal | Diagnosis | Action |\n|--------|-----------|--------|\n| Stale heartbeat + PID dead | **Crashed.** Worker terminated unexpectedly. | Release claim, clean up, emit `peer.crashed` |\n| Stale heartbeat + PID alive | **Stuck.** Worker is hung (deadlock, infinite loop, blocked I/O). | Emit `peer.stale` warning. Do NOT kill — may be legitimately slow. Alert via Knot after threshold. |\n| Fresh heartbeat + PID alive | **Healthy.** Normal operation. | No action. |\n\n**NEEDLE does not auto-kill stuck workers.** A stuck worker with a live PID may be executing a legitimately slow agent. Killing it would interrupt work. Instead, NEEDLE alerts via Knot and lets the human decide.\n\n## Database Recovery\n\nbeads_rust uses SQLite with a known corruption issue (FrankenSQLite, upstream #171). NEEDLE must handle this.\n\n### Recovery Procedure\n\n```\nCorruption detected\n       │\n       ▼\n  Run br doctor --repair\n       │\n       ├── Success ──► Resume operation, emit health.db_repaired\n       │\n       └── Failure ──► Full rebuild:\n                          1. rm .beads/beads.db\n                          2. br sync --import\n                          3. Verify: br doctor\n                          │\n                          ├── Success ──► Resume, emit health.db_rebuilt\n                          │\n                          └── Failure ──► ERRORED state (JSONL itself may be corrupt)\n```\n\n**Key insight from `docs/notes/mitosis-explosion-postmortem.md`:** The JSONL file is always the authoritative data source. It is append-only and immune to SQLite corruption. Recovery always rebuilds from JSONL.\n\n### Proactive Health Checks\n\nThe Mend strand runs `br doctor` (without `--repair`) periodically:\n- After every N beads processed (configurable, default: 50)\n- On every Mend strand evaluation\n- If doctor reports warnings, escalate to `--repair` immediately rather than waiting for failure\n\n## Stale Claim Recovery\n\n```\nMend strand evaluates:\n  1. Query beads with status=in_progress\n  2. For each:\n     a. Read assigned worker ID from bead\n     b. Check worker's heartbeat file\n     c. If heartbeat is stale AND PID is dead:\n        - br update <bead_id> --status open --unassign\n        - Emit bead.released telemetry (reason: stale_claim)\n     d. If heartbeat is stale AND PID is alive:\n        - Emit peer.stale warning (do not release — worker may be slow)\n     e. If heartbeat is fresh:\n        - Normal operation, skip\n```\n\nA claimed bead is only released if the owning worker is **confirmed dead** (stale heartbeat AND dead PID). If the PID is alive, the bead is not released, even if the heartbeat is stale.\n\n## Lock File Recovery\n\nMend strand checks lock file age:\n1. Read lock files in `/tmp/needle-claim-*.lock`\n2. If file modification time > `lock_ttl` (default: 10 minutes):\n   - Attempt to acquire flock (non-blocking)\n   - If acquired: no one holds it, delete the file, release flock\n   - If not acquired: someone is actively holding it, skip\n\n## Dependency Link Recovery\n\nMend strand checks for stale dependencies:\n1. Query beads with status `open` that have blockers\n2. For each blocker, check if the blocking bead is closed\n3. If blocker is closed, remove the dependency link\n4. Emit `bead.dependency.cleaned` telemetry\n\nThis is a necessary compensating mechanism because `br` does not automatically resolve dependency links on bead closure (documented in `docs/notes/bead-lifecycle-bugs.md`).\n\n## Graceful Degradation\n\nWhen subsystems fail, NEEDLE degrades gracefully rather than crashing:\n\n| Subsystem Failure | Degradation |\n|-------------------|-------------|\n| Telemetry file sink unwritable | Buffer events in memory, retry. If buffer full, drop events. Worker continues. |\n| Heartbeat file unwritable | Log error. Worker continues but cannot be monitored by peers. If persistent, ERRORED. |\n| Worker registry unwritable | Log error. Worker continues but invisible to `needle list`. |\n| Database corrupt | Auto-repair. If repair fails, ERRORED for that workspace only. |\n| Single workspace unreachable | Skip workspace in Explore, continue with others. |\n| Config file unreadable mid-session | Use cached config from boot. Emit warning. |\n\n## Self-Modification and Release Channels\n\nNEEDLE workers are allowed to modify NEEDLE itself. The v1 failures (see `docs/notes/self-modification-risks.md`) were not caused by self-modification as a concept — they were caused by untested changes deploying directly to the running fleet. The solution is not to ban self-modification but to gate promotion through release channels with canary testing.\n\n### Release Channels\n\n```\n:testing ──► :stable ──► fleet hot-reload\n                │\n                └── rollback to previous :stable on failure\n```\n\nThree channels:\n\n| Channel | Purpose | Who writes | Who reads |\n|---------|---------|------------|-----------|\n| `:testing` | Newly built binary, not yet validated | Worker that built it | Canary test harness only |\n| `:stable` | Validated binary, approved for fleet use | Promotion pipeline (after canary passes) | Running fleet via hot-reload |\n| `:latest` | Alias for the most recent `:stable` | Automatic on promotion | `needle upgrade` default target |\n\n### Canary Testing Pipeline\n\nWhen a worker modifies NEEDLE's source and builds a new binary:\n\n```\nWorker builds new binary\n       │\n       ▼\n  Install as :testing\n  (~/.needle/bin/needle-testing)\n       │\n       ▼\n  Run canary test suite:\n    1. Launch :testing binary with test .beads/ directory\n    2. Test beads have defined inputs and expected outcomes\n    3. :testing processes beads in isolation\n    4. Compare actual outcomes against expected\n       │\n       ├── All pass → Promote :testing to :stable\n       │                 │\n       │                 ▼\n       │              Fleet detects new :stable\n       │              Workers hot-reload on next bead boundary\n       │\n       └── Any fail → Reject :testing\n                        │\n                        ▼\n                     Mark bead as failed\n                     :stable remains unchanged\n                     Fleet continues on previous :stable\n                     Emit canary.failed telemetry\n```\n\n### Canary Test Suite\n\nThe canary suite is a set of test beads with known-good outcomes stored in a dedicated test workspace:\n\n```\n~/.needle/canary/\n├── .beads/                    # test bead store\n│   ├── issues.jsonl\n│   └── beads.db\n├── test-workspace/            # mock workspace with source files\n│   ├── src/\n│   │   └── hello.py           # simple file for beads to modify\n│   └── .beads/\n└── expected/                  # expected outcomes per bead\n    ├── bead-001.expected.json # { \"exit_code\": 0, \"bead_closed\": true }\n    ├── bead-002.expected.json # { \"exit_code\": 0, \"files_modified\": [\"src/hello.py\"] }\n    └── bead-003.expected.json # { \"exit_code\": 1, \"bead_closed\": false }\n```\n\nTest beads cover:\n- **Happy path:** Simple bead that should succeed and close\n- **Failure path:** Bead that should fail (tests outcome handling)\n- **Timeout path:** Bead with intentionally slow agent (tests timeout enforcement)\n- **State machine integrity:** Verify telemetry events match expected state transitions\n- **Mitosis:** Multi-task bead that should split on failure\n\n### Hot-Reload Protocol\n\nRunning workers check for a new `:stable` binary between bead processing cycles (after LOGGING, before SELECTING):\n\n1. Compare current binary hash against `:stable` binary hash\n2. If different:\n   a. Emit `worker.upgrade.detected` telemetry\n   b. Complete current bead cycle (never interrupt mid-execution)\n   c. Re-exec with the new binary: `exec ~/.needle/bin/needle-stable run --resume`\n   d. New binary picks up worker state from heartbeat file and registry\n3. If same: continue normally\n\n**`--resume` flag:** Tells the new binary to inherit the worker's identity (ID, session, tmux) rather than creating a new session. The worker continues from the SELECTING state with a fresh binary.\n\n### Rollback\n\nIf a promoted `:stable` causes failures in the fleet:\n\n1. Fleet workers emit `worker.errored` or repeated `outcome.failure` telemetry\n2. Human (or automated watchdog) runs: `needle rollback`\n3. Rollback restores the previous `:stable` from backup (`~/.needle/bin/needle-stable.prev`)\n4. Workers hot-reload to the rolled-back binary on next cycle\n\nRollback is always available because promotion preserves the previous `:stable` as a backup.\n\n### Binary Paths\n\n```\n~/.needle/bin/\n├── needle-testing             # candidate under canary evaluation\n├── needle-stable              # current fleet binary\n├── needle-stable.prev         # previous stable (rollback target)\n└── needle                     # symlink → needle-stable\n```\n\n### Configuration\n\n```yaml\nself_modification:\n  enabled: true                     # allow workers to process NEEDLE beads\n  canary_workspace: ~/.needle/canary  # test workspace with known-good beads\n  auto_promote: true                # promote to :stable automatically if canary passes\n  hot_reload: true                  # fleet hot-reloads from :stable between beads\n```\n\n### Telemetry\n\n| Event Type | Emitted When | Data Fields |\n|------------|-------------|-------------|\n| `canary.started` | Canary test suite begins | `testing_binary_hash`, `test_count` |\n| `canary.passed` | All canary tests passed | `testing_binary_hash`, `duration_ms` |\n| `canary.failed` | One or more canary tests failed | `testing_binary_hash`, `failures` (list) |\n| `promotion.completed` | :testing promoted to :stable | `old_hash`, `new_hash` |\n| `worker.upgrade.detected` | Worker sees new :stable | `old_hash`, `new_hash` |\n| `worker.upgrade.completed` | Worker re-exec'd with new binary | `new_hash` |\n| `rollback.completed` | :stable rolled back to previous | `rolled_back_hash`, `restored_hash` |\n\n---\n\n# Configuration\n\nNEEDLE uses a hierarchical configuration system. Values are resolved from highest to lowest precedence, with the first defined value winning.\n\n## Precedence Order\n\n```\nCLI arguments          (highest — overrides everything)\n       │\nEnvironment variables\n       │\nWorkspace config       (.needle.yaml in workspace root)\n       │\nGlobal config          (~/.needle/config.yaml)\n       │\nBuilt-in defaults      (lowest — always present)\n```\n\n**Rule:** A value set at a higher level completely replaces the lower level's value. There is no deep merging. For maps (like `strands`), the entire map is replaced, not merged key-by-key.\n\n**Exception:** The `workspaces` list in Explore strand config is additive — workspace configs can add to the global list but not remove from it.\n\n## Global Configuration\n\n**Location:** `~/.needle/config.yaml`\n\n```yaml\n# ── Agent Configuration ──\nagent:\n  default: claude-anthropic-sonnet\n  timeout: 600\n  adapters_dir: ~/.needle/agents\n\n# ── Worker Configuration ──\nworker:\n  max_workers: 0                      # 0 = no hard ceiling, rely on runtime monitoring\n  launch_stagger_seconds: 2\n  idle_timeout: 300\n  idle_action: wait\n  max_claim_retries: 5\n  identifier_scheme: nato\n  cpu_load_warn: 0.8                  # warn when load > 80% of cores\n  memory_free_warn_mb: 512            # warn when free RAM < 512MB\n\n# ── Workspace Configuration ──\nworkspace:\n  default: ~/projects/main\n  home: ~/projects/main\n\n# ── Strand Configuration ──\nstrands:\n  pluck:\n    enabled: true\n    exclude_labels: [deferred, human, blocked]\n  explore:\n    enabled: true\n    workspaces:\n      - ~/projects/api-server\n      - ~/projects/frontend\n  mend:\n    enabled: true\n    stale_claim_ttl: 300\n    lock_ttl: 600\n    db_check_interval: 50\n  weave:\n    enabled: false\n    max_beads_per_run: 5\n    cooldown_hours: 24\n    exclude_workspaces: []\n  unravel:\n    enabled: false\n    max_per_run: 3\n    cooldown_days: 7\n  pulse:\n    enabled: false\n    max_beads_per_run: 10\n    cooldown_hours: 48\n    severity_threshold: warning\n    scanners: []\n  knot:\n    enabled: true\n    alert_cooldown_minutes: 60\n    exhaustion_threshold: 3\n\n# ── Concurrency Limits ──\nlimits:\n  providers:\n    anthropic:\n      max_concurrent: 10\n      requests_per_minute: 60\n    openai:\n      max_concurrent: 5\n      requests_per_minute: 40\n  models: {}\n\n# ── Health Monitoring ──\nhealth:\n  heartbeat_interval: 30\n  heartbeat_ttl: 300\n  peer_check_interval: 60\n\n# ── Telemetry ──\ntelemetry:\n  file_sink:\n    enabled: true\n    directory: ~/.needle/logs\n    rotation: session\n    retention_days: 30\n  stdout_sink:\n    enabled: false\n    format: normal\n    color: auto\n  hooks: []\n  otlp:\n    enabled: false\n    endpoint: \"http://localhost:4317\"\n    protocol: grpc              # grpc | http/protobuf\n    headers: {}                 # e.g., authorization: \"Bearer ${OTEL_TOKEN}\"\n    timeout_ms: 5000\n    compression: gzip           # none | gzip\n    tls:\n      insecure: false\n      ca_file: \"\"\n    signals:\n      traces: true\n      metrics: true\n      logs: true\n    resource_attributes:\n      deployment.environment: \"development\"\n      service.namespace: \"needle-fleet\"\n\n# ── Cost Tracking ──\npricing: {}\nbudget:\n  warn_usd: 0\n  stop_usd: 0\n\n# ── Self-Modification & Release Channels ──\nself_modification:\n  enabled: true\n  canary_workspace: ~/.needle/canary\n  auto_promote: true\n  hot_reload: true\n```\n\n## Workspace Configuration\n\n**Location:** `.needle.yaml` in workspace root (next to `.beads/`)\n\nWorkspace-level configuration overrides global settings for that specific workspace. Only a subset of settings can be overridden at the workspace level.\n\n```yaml\nagent:\n  default: claude-anthropic-opus\n  timeout: 1200\n\nstrands:\n  weave:\n    enabled: true\n    max_beads_per_run: 3\n  pulse:\n    enabled: true\n    scanners:\n      - name: rust-clippy\n        command: \"cargo clippy --message-format=json 2>/dev/null\"\n\nprompt:\n  context_files:\n    - AGENTS.md\n    - docs/architecture.md\n  instructions: |\n    This workspace uses the repository pattern.\n    All database access must go through src/repository/.\n    Run `cargo test` before closing the bead.\n```\n\n### Overridable Settings\n\n| Setting | Workspace Override | Why |\n|---------|-------------------|-----|\n| `agent.default` | Yes | Different projects may need different models |\n| `agent.timeout` | Yes | Complex projects may need longer timeouts |\n| `strands.weave` | Yes | Some projects want gap analysis, others don't |\n| `strands.pulse` | Yes | Scanners are project-specific |\n| `strands.unravel` | Yes | Per-project opt-in |\n| `prompt.*` | Yes | Project-specific context and instructions |\n| `worker.*` | **No** | Worker config is fleet-level, not per-workspace |\n| `limits.*` | **No** | Rate limits are provider-level, not per-workspace |\n| `health.*` | **No** | Health monitoring is fleet-level |\n| `telemetry.*` | **No** | Telemetry config is fleet-level |\n\n## Environment Variables\n\nAll configuration keys can be overridden via environment variables with the `NEEDLE_` prefix. Nested keys use `__` (double underscore) as separator.\n\n| Config Key | Environment Variable |\n|------------|---------------------|\n| `agent.default` | `NEEDLE_AGENT__DEFAULT` |\n| `agent.timeout` | `NEEDLE_AGENT__TIMEOUT` |\n| `worker.max_workers` | `NEEDLE_WORKER__MAX_WORKERS` |\n| `strands.weave.enabled` | `NEEDLE_STRANDS__WEAVE__ENABLED` |\n\n## Configuration Validation\n\nConfiguration is validated at boot time. Invalid configuration causes the worker to enter ERRORED state immediately.\n\n### Required Fields\n\n- `agent.default` must reference a valid adapter (built-in or file exists in adapters dir)\n- `workspace.default` or `--workspace` must be a directory containing `.beads/`\n- Numeric fields must be positive\n- Duration fields must be > 0\n\n### Warnings (non-fatal)\n\n- `worker.max_workers` > 0 and > CPU count (consider runtime monitoring instead)\n- `health.heartbeat_ttl` < `3 * health.heartbeat_interval` (detection may be unreliable)\n- `strands.explore.workspaces` contains paths that don't exist\n- No pricing configured when `telemetry.effort.track_cost: true`\n\n### Config Dump\n\n```bash\nneedle config --dump\nneedle config --dump --show-source\n\n# Example output:\n# agent.default: claude-anthropic-sonnet (from: ~/.needle/config.yaml)\n# agent.timeout: 1200 (from: /home/coder/project/.needle.yaml)\n# worker.max_workers: 20 (from: NEEDLE_WORKER__MAX_WORKERS env var)\n# worker.idle_timeout: 300 (from: built-in default)\n```\n\n---\n\n# Agent Adapters\n\nNEEDLE is agent-agnostic. It wraps any headless CLI that accepts a prompt and exits. The adapter system is the abstraction layer that makes this possible.\n\nNEEDLE does not know how agents work. It knows how to:\n1. Render an invoke template with variables\n2. Pipe a prompt via the configured input method\n3. Wait for the process to exit\n4. Capture exit code, stdout, and stderr\n\nEverything else — authentication, model selection, context handling, tool use — is the agent's responsibility.\n\n## Adapter Interface\n\nAn adapter is a YAML file that describes how to invoke a specific agent:\n\n```yaml\nname: claude-anthropic-sonnet\ndescription: Claude Code with Anthropic Sonnet model\nagent_cli: claude\nversion_command: \"claude --version\"\ninput_method: stdin                   # stdin | file | args\ninvoke_template: >\n  cd {workspace} &&\n  claude --print\n  --model claude-sonnet-4-6\n  --max-turns 30\n  --output-format json\n  < {prompt_file}\nenvironment:\n  CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TURNS: \"30\"\ntoken_extraction:\n  method: json_field                  # json_field | regex | none\n  input_path: \"usage.input_tokens\"\n  output_path: \"usage.output_tokens\"\nprovider: anthropic\nmodel: claude-sonnet-4-6\n```\n\n## Input Methods\n\n### stdin\n\nPrompt is piped to the agent's stdin. Most common for Claude Code. NEEDLE writes the prompt to a temp file (`{prompt_file}`) and redirects it to stdin to avoid shell escaping issues.\n\n### file\n\nPrompt is written to a file and the file path is passed as an argument.\n\n### args\n\nPrompt is passed as a command-line argument. `{prompt_escaped}` is the prompt with shell metacharacters escaped. For long prompts, NEEDLE may fall back to file-based input.\n\n## Template Variables\n\n| Variable | Description | Example |\n|----------|-------------|---------|\n| `{workspace}` | Absolute path to workspace | `/home/coder/project` |\n| `{prompt_file}` | Path to temp file containing the prompt | `/tmp/needle-prompt-a1b2.txt` |\n| `{prompt_escaped}` | Shell-escaped prompt string | `Fix the auth bug in src/auth.rs` |\n| `{bead_id}` | Current bead ID | `nd-a3f8` |\n| `{model}` | Model identifier from adapter config | `claude-sonnet-4-6` |\n| `{worker_id}` | Worker identifier | `needle-claude-anthropic-sonnet-alpha` |\n| `{timeout}` | Timeout in seconds | `600` |\n\n## Built-in Adapters\n\nNEEDLE ships with adapters for common agents, embedded in the binary. These can be overridden by placing a file with the same name in `~/.needle/agents/`.\n\n### Claude Code (Sonnet)\n\n```yaml\nname: claude-anthropic-sonnet\nagent_cli: claude\ninput_method: stdin\ninvoke_template: >\n  cd {workspace} && claude --print --model claude-sonnet-4-6\n  --max-turns 30 --output-format json --verbose < {prompt_file}\ntoken_extraction:\n  method: json_field\n  input_path: \"result.usage.input_tokens\"\n  output_path: \"result.usage.output_tokens\"\nprovider: anthropic\nmodel: claude-sonnet-4-6\n```\n\n### Claude Code (Opus)\n\n```yaml\nname: claude-anthropic-opus\nagent_cli: claude\ninput_method: stdin\ninvoke_template: >\n  cd {workspace} && claude --print --model claude-opus-4-6\n  --max-turns 50 --output-format json --verbose < {prompt_file}\ntoken_extraction:\n  method: json_field\n  input_path: \"result.usage.input_tokens\"\n  output_path: \"result.usage.output_tokens\"\nprovider: anthropic\nmodel: claude-opus-4-6\n```\n\n### OpenCode\n\n```yaml\nname: opencode-default\nagent_cli: opencode\ninput_method: file\ninvoke_template: >\n  cd {workspace} && opencode run --prompt-file {prompt_file} --non-interactive\ntoken_extraction:\n  method: none\nprovider: configurable\nmodel: configurable\n```\n\n### Codex CLI\n\n```yaml\nname: codex-openai-gpt4\nagent_cli: codex\ninput_method: args\ninvoke_template: >\n  cd {workspace} && codex --model gpt-4 --approval-mode full-auto \"{prompt_escaped}\"\ntoken_extraction:\n  method: none\nprovider: openai\nmodel: gpt-4\n```\n\n### Aider\n\n```yaml\nname: aider-anthropic-sonnet\nagent_cli: aider\ninput_method: args\ninvoke_template: >\n  cd {workspace} && aider --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --yes --message \"{prompt_escaped}\"\ntoken_extraction:\n  method: regex\n  pattern: \"Tokens: ([\\\\d,]+) sent, ([\\\\d,]+) received\"\n  input_group: 1\n  output_group: 2\nprovider: anthropic\nmodel: claude-sonnet-4-6\n```\n\n## Prompt Templates\n\nPrompts are configurable at both the global and workspace level. Every agent-invoking operation (Pluck execution, Weave gap analysis, Unravel alternatives, Pulse scanning, Mitosis splitting) uses a named prompt template. Templates are deterministic functions of their inputs — same bead state produces the same prompt.\n\n### Template Variables\n\nAll templates have access to these variables:\n\n| Variable | Available In | Description |\n|----------|-------------|-------------|\n| `{bead_id}` | All | Current bead ID |\n| `{bead_title}` | All | Bead title |\n| `{bead_body}` | All | Bead body/description |\n| `{workspace_path}` | All | Absolute path to workspace |\n| `{context_file_contents}` | All | Contents of configured context files |\n| `{workspace_instructions}` | All | Instructions from `.needle.yaml` |\n| `{worker_id}` | All | Worker identifier |\n| `{existing_children}` | Mitosis | Parent's current children (titles + IDs) |\n| `{human_bead_context}` | Unravel | The HUMAN-blocked bead being analyzed |\n| `{scan_results}` | Pulse | Output from configured scanners |\n| `{doc_files}` | Weave | Documentation file listing and contents |\n\n### Built-in Templates\n\n**`pluck` — Bead execution (default):**\n\n```markdown\n## Task\n\n{bead_title}\n\n## Description\n\n{bead_body}\n\n## Workspace\n\n{workspace_path}\n\n## Context Files\n\n{context_file_contents}\n\n## Instructions\n\n{workspace_instructions}\n\nComplete the task described above. When finished:\n- Commit your changes with a descriptive message\n- Close the bead: `br close {bead_id} --body \"Summary of what was done\"`\n\nIf you cannot complete the task:\n- Do NOT close the bead\n- The bead will be automatically released for retry\n\nBead ID: {bead_id}\n```\n\n**`mitosis` — Split analysis:**\n\n```markdown\n## Bead Analysis\n\nTitle: {bead_title}\nBody: {bead_body}\n\n## Existing Children\n\n{existing_children}\n\n## Question\n\nDoes this bead describe more than one independent task? A task is independent\nif it produces a distinct deliverable and could be completed without completing\nthe other tasks in this bead.\n\nIf yes, list each independent task as a structured child bead with:\n- title: concise task description\n- body: what needs to be done\n- dependencies: which other children must complete first (by title)\n\nIf this bead describes a single task (even a complex one), respond with: SINGLE_TASK\n\nDo not propose children that duplicate any existing children listed above.\n```\n\n**`weave` — Gap analysis:**\n\n```markdown\n## Workspace Documentation\n\n{doc_files}\n\n## Current Open Beads\n\n{existing_beads}\n\n## Question\n\nReview the documentation above. Identify gaps where documented features,\nAPIs, or workflows are incomplete, missing tests, or have no corresponding\nimplementation bead.\n\nFor each gap found, propose a bead with:\n- title: concise description of what's missing\n- body: what needs to be done to close the gap\n- priority: 1 (critical), 2 (important), or 3 (nice-to-have)\n\nDo not propose beads that duplicate any existing open beads listed above.\nIf no gaps are found, respond with: NO_GAPS\n```\n\n**`unravel` — Alternative proposals:**\n\n```markdown\n## Blocked Bead\n\nTitle: {bead_title}\nBody: {bead_body}\nStatus: Blocked (requires human decision)\n\n## Question\n\nThis bead is blocked because it requires a human decision. Analyze the bead\nand propose alternative approaches that could be executed by an automated\nagent without the human decision.\n\nFor each alternative, provide:\n- title: concise description of the alternative approach\n- body: what would be done differently\n- tradeoffs: what is gained and what is lost compared to the original approach\n\nIf no viable alternatives exist, respond with: NO_ALTERNATIVES\n```\n\n**`pulse` — Health scan bead creation:**\n\n```markdown\n## Scan Results\n\n{scan_results}\n\n## Current Open Beads\n\n{existing_beads}\n\n## Question\n\nReview the scan results above. For issues that are significant enough to\nwarrant a fix, propose a bead with:\n- title: concise description of the issue\n- body: what needs to be fixed and how\n- priority: based on severity (1=critical, 2=important, 3=minor)\n\nDo not propose beads that duplicate any existing open beads listed above.\nIf no significant issues are found, respond with: NO_ISSUES\n```\n\n### Overriding Templates\n\nTemplates are overridable at the workspace level in `.needle.yaml`:\n\n```yaml\nprompt:\n  context_files:\n    - CLAUDE.md\n    - AGENTS.md\n  instructions: |\n    This workspace uses the repository pattern.\n    Run `cargo test` before closing the bead.\n\n  templates:\n    pluck: |\n      {bead_title}\n\n      {bead_body}\n\n      Workspace: {workspace_path}\n      {context_file_contents}\n      {workspace_instructions}\n\n      Close when done: br close {bead_id} --body \"summary\"\n      Bead ID: {bead_id}\n\n    mitosis: |\n      ... custom mitosis prompt ...\n```\n\nIf a template is not overridden at the workspace level, the built-in default is used. Templates can also be overridden globally in `~/.needle/config.yaml` under `prompt.templates`.\n\n### Agent-Owned Closure\n\nThe pluck template instructs the agent to close the bead via `br close`. NEEDLE does not close beads itself. This is a deliberate design decision based on v1 experience:\n\n- The agent knows whether the work is actually done\n- NEEDLE's post-dispatch parsing of agent output was fragile\n- Exit code 0 does not guarantee the work was completed correctly\n- The agent can include a meaningful closure message\n\n## Adapter Validation\n\n```bash\nneedle test-agent claude-anthropic-sonnet\n\n# Output:\n#   Adapter: claude-anthropic-sonnet\n#   CLI:     claude (found at /home/coder/.local/bin/claude)\n#   Version: Claude Code v1.0.30\n#   Input:   stdin\n#   Probe:   echo hello → exit 0 (1.2s)\n#   Tokens:  extraction working (in: 45, out: 12)\n#   Status:  READY\n```\n\n## Adding a Custom Agent\n\n1. Create a YAML file in `~/.needle/agents/`\n2. Edit the file with the agent's invocation details\n3. Test the adapter: `needle test-agent my-agent`\n4. Use it: `needle run --agent my-agent`\n\nNo code changes required. No recompilation. No restart of other workers.\n\n---\n\n# Implementation Phases\n\nNEEDLE is built in three phases. Each phase produces a usable tool. No phase depends on future phases — Phase 1 alone is a complete, working system.\n\n## Phase 1: Core State Machine\n\n**Goal:** A single binary that processes beads from one workspace using one agent. The state machine is complete. Telemetry is complete. The tool works end-to-end.\n\n### Deliverables\n\n| Component | Scope |\n|-----------|-------|\n| **CLI** | `needle run`, `needle stop`, `needle list`, `needle version` |\n| **Worker** | Full state machine: BOOTING → SELECTING → CLAIMING → BUILDING → DISPATCHING → EXECUTING → HANDLING → LOGGING → (loop) |\n| **Strand 1 (Pluck)** | Query, filter, sort beads from single workspace |\n| **Strand 7 (Knot)** | Basic exhaustion handling (backoff, exit) |\n| **Claimer** | Atomic claim via `br update --claim`, single workspace flock |\n| **PromptBuilder** | Deterministic prompt from bead context |\n| **Dispatcher** | Agent adapter loading, process execution, timeout enforcement |\n| **OutcomeHandler** | All 6 outcomes handled (success, failure, timeout, crash, agent_not_found, interrupted) |\n| **Telemetry** | File sink (JSONL), all events in catalog |\n| **Config** | Global config file, CLI argument overrides |\n| **Agent adapters** | Claude Code built-in, generic template |\n| **BeadStore** | `br` CLI wrapper with JSON parsing |","numLines":1000,"startLine":1966,"totalLines":3988}}}

However, **worker-level filtering happens AFTER the strand returns**.\n\n### The Deadlock\nIf a workspace has candidates but they are all:\n1. **Excluded** - Already attempted and failed within the race-lost TTL (30s)\n2. **Already assigned** - Assigned to other workers\n\nThen:\n1. `ExploreStrand::evaluate()` returns `StrandResult::BeadFound(candidates)` \n2. The claiming code filters by exclusions and assignees\n3. Zero beads remain claimable\n4. Worker enters idle backoff (observed at **900s**)\n5. Loop repeats, never advancing to workspace #2\n\n### Real-World Impact\n**2026-07-11 lab incident:**\n- 24 ready beads across 24 workspaces (one per workspace)\n- 4 roaming workers available\n- Throughput: **~1 bead per 40 minutes**\n- Same pinned workers processed **hundreds of beads** in the same period\n\n### Root Causes (from ADR-001)\n\n1. **Return-on-first-candidates deadlock** - `evaluate()` returns at first workspace with ready candidates, but unclaimable filtering happens later\n2. **Thundering herd** - All workers walk the same list in the same order, all converge on the same store\n3. **Store-layer limit bugs** - No `--limit` passed (truncates output) or `--limit 0` (returns empty)\n4. **Stale assignees are permanent** - `reopen` doesn't clear assignee; cross-workspace mend only handles orphans\n5. **Claim errors masquerade as races** - CLI failures collapse into `claimed_by=(race)`\n6. **Boot-only discovery** - New stores require worker restarts\n\n## Proposed Fix Approach (Phase 5 Plan)\n\n### 5.1 Selection Correctness\n\n**Claimable-aware candidate filtering:**\n- Pass worker exclusion state into the strand's `Filters`\n- Scan advancement driven by **claimable-by-me** candidates, not just \"ready\" candidates\n- Loop advances past workspaces with nothing claimable by this worker\n\n**Per-worker scan rotation:**\n- Start iteration at `hash(qualified_id) % N`, wrapping around\n- Workers partition the workspace list instead of racing for the same first store\n\n**Store-layer limit correctness:**\n- Always pass explicit large limit to `br ready --json`\n- Add boot-time `bf --version` handshake that WARNs on known-bad versions\n\n### 5.2 Stale-State Healing\n\n**Mend releases stale assignees on open beads:**\n- Extend cross-workspace mend to handle open beads with dead assignees\n- Clear assignees when the assigned worker has no live heartbeat\n\n**Claim-error taxonomy:**\n- Distinguish error from race in claim results\n- After N consecutive errors, emit ERROR telemetry and mark bead/store suspect\n\n### 5.3 Cadence and Liveness\n\n**Event-driven wakeups + jittered floor:**\n- Replace flat idle backoff (900s) with mtime/inotify watches on `.beads/issues.jsonl`\n- Jittered 60-120s polling floor\n- Found-but-excluded triggers short retry, never idle backoff\n\n**Periodic re-discovery:**\n- Re-run workspace discovery every N cycles\n- No upward traversal constraint remains\n\n### 5.4 Observability\n\n**Per-cycle scan telemetry:**\n- Workspaces visited\n- Candidates found\n- Exclusion reasons\n\n**Starvation alarm:**\n- Ready beads exist but worker claimed nothing for X minutes\n- Surface last-scan-per-workspace in `needle status`\n\n## Code Evidence\n\nFrom `src/strand/explore.rs` (current implementation):\n\n```rust\n// Line 156-163: Filters don't include worker exclusions\nlet filters = Filters {\n    assignee: None,  // ← Only filters by assignee=None\n    exclude_labels: vec![\n        \"deferred\".to_string(),\n        \"human\".to_string(),\n        \"blocked\".to_string(),\n    ],\n};\n\n// Line 191-194: Query happens BEFORE worker-level filtering\nmatch filters, but the worker's exclusion set (race-lost beads) is never passed down.
